definition_zh: 色谱（法）的；用色谱法分离、检测或分析的
definition_en: relating to chromatography, the technique of separating the components of a mixture by passing them through a medium at different speeds
core_image: 一滴植物浸液点在滤纸下缘，溶剂向上爬，颜色被拉成几条长短不一的横带，像有人用颜色写了一行字
scene: 实验台上，一片绿叶的浸液被点在滤纸下缘，溶剂沿着纸面往上爬，颜色慢慢分成几条深浅不同的横带。The chromatographic separation revealed four pigments in the leaf extract.
sceneCN: 这里 chromatographic 指「用色谱法进行的分离」（第 1 个义项：与色谱分离方法相关）；句意为这次色谱分离在叶片提取液里显示出四种色素。图中可辨识物件：滤纸、点样毛细管、展开槽、四条色带。

pos.zh: 色谱（法）的；用色谱法分离或检测的

senses.title: Belonging to the separation method
senses.definition: relating to chromatography as a laboratory technique for separating mixtures
senses.definitionCN: 与作为分离混合物的实验室技术的色谱法有关
senses.example: The team chose a chromatographic method to separate the leaf pigments.
senses.exampleCN: 团队选择用色谱方法分离叶片中的色素。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the name of the technique to whatever it describes, so this is its plainest reading.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把技术名称挂到所修饰的对象上，因此这是它最朴素的用法。

senses.title: Produced by a chromatographic run
senses.titleCN: 由色谱分离得到的结果
senses.definition: obtained as a fraction or result of a chromatographic separation
senses.definitionCN: 作为色谱分离的馏分或结果而得到的
senses.example: The chromatographic fraction held a single sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 这一色谱馏分中只含一种糖。
senses.why: Once a mixture has been run through the medium, whatever comes out carries the name of the process that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 混合物一旦通过介质跑完一遍，出来的东西就带上产生它的那道工序之名。

senses.title: Naming the apparatus of the method
senses.titleCN: 指称色谱法所用装置的
senses.definition: describing a column, plate, detector or instrument built for chromatography
senses.definitionCN: 描述为色谱法而制造的柱、板、检测器或仪器
senses.example: She changed the chromatographic column before the next run.
senses.exampleCN: 在下一次进样前，她换掉了色谱柱。
senses.why: Apparatus takes the adjective because the column exists only in order to perform this one operation.
senses.whyCN: 装置带上这个形容词，是因为色谱柱存在的唯一目的就是完成这一道操作。

senses.title: Read as a pattern of peaks
senses.definition: describing a trace, profile or fingerprint that records the separated components as peaks
senses.definitionCN: 描述把已分离组分记成峰形的图谱、轮廓或指纹
senses.example: The chromatographic profile showed one unexpected peak.
senses.exampleCN: 色谱图谱上出现了一个意料之外的峰。
senses.why: The record left by the run is a picture of separation, so it inherits the adjective from the process.
senses.whyCN: 一次分离留下的记录就是分离本身的图像，因此它也从这一过程继承了该形容词。

senses.title: Spread out in visible bands
senses.titleCN: 呈层层展开色带的（视觉比喻）
senses.definition: used of a visual effect in which colours or layers spread apart in bands, like a developed chromatogram
senses.definitionCN: 用于颜色或层次像显影后的色谱图那样分成带状铺开的视觉效果
senses.example: The ink spread into a chromatographic fan across the wet paper.
senses.exampleCN: 墨水在湿纸上散成一个扇形的色带。
senses.why: The technique began with coloured pigments, so its visual signature of banded spreading became a ready comparison outside the lab.
senses.whyCN: 这门技术最初处理的是彩色色素，于是「分层铺开」的视觉特征就成了实验室之外的现成比喻。

senses.title: Of a grade fit for the method
senses.definition: describing a solvent or standard purified to the level that chromatography requires
senses.definitionCN: 描述纯化到色谱分析所要求程度的溶剂或标准品
senses.example: Only chromatographic grade solvent was used for the trace analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 痕量分析只使用了色谱级溶剂。
senses.why: A method sensitive to traces forces everything used in it to be cleaned to the same standard, and the adjective marks that standard.
senses.whyCN: 对痕量敏感的方法会迫使所用一切都被净化到同一标准，这个形容词就标出那一标准。

senses.title: Able to split a mixture into parts
senses.titleCN: 能把混杂局面拆开的（抽象义）
senses.definition: used figuratively of an approach that separates a tangled mixture of things into distinct parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻把纠缠在一起的混杂局面拆成若干清楚部分的做法
senses.example: The committee took a chromatographic approach to the flood of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会用一种「色谱式」的办法处理涌入的投诉。
senses.why: The abstract use keeps only the core gesture of the method, namely sorting one mass into several separable parts.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法只保留方法的核心动作，即把一团东西分拣成几个可以分开的部分。

senses.title: Of the literal colour-writing name
senses.definition: referring to the literal sense of the coined name, writing or recording by means of colour
senses.definitionCN: 指这个新造名称的字面义，即借助颜色来书写或记录
senses.example: The name itself preserves a chromatographic idea: writing with colour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名称本身就保留着「用颜色书写」的意象。
senses.why: The word was coined from a Greek noun for colour and a Greek verb for writing, and this literal layer still shows through the technical adjective.
senses.whyCN: 该词由希腊语中表示颜色的名词与表示书写的动词合成，这层字面意思至今仍透在这个技术形容词里。

intro.en: The adjective comes from the name of the technique, coined in the early twentieth century from Greek khrōma 'colour' and graphein 'to write'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词来自技术名称本身，该名称于二十世纪初由希腊语表示「颜色」的名词与表示「书写」的动词合成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Khrōma meant 'colour', and also 'skin, surface'. It is generally connected with khrōs 'skin, complexion', though the exact pre-Greek shape is a reconstruction.
items.cn: khrōma 意为「颜色」，也指「皮肤、表面」。一般认为它与表示「肤色、面色」的 khrōs 相关，但其希腊语之前的确切形态属重构形式。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to scratch, draw, write', and gave the combining element -graphia 'writing, recording'. Its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: graphein 意为「刻、画、写」，并提供了表示「书写、记录」的组合成分。其更深来源没有定论。

items.en: A Russian botanist used the new Latin name chromatographia around the turn of the twentieth century for a method that separated plant pigments into coloured bands on paper. First date uncertain (exact year of coining): the first publication date is variously given, so the precise year is not fixed here.
items.cn: 一位俄国植物学家在二十世纪之交用新拉丁名称 chromatographia 指一种把植物色素在纸上分成色带的方法。首见年代不确定：首次发表的年份各家说法不一，此处不锁定具体年份。

items.en: English took the noun as chromatography, and within a few decades the derived adjective was in use in chemical writing.
items.cn: 英语以表示该技术的名词吸收了这个名称，几十年内其派生形容词就出现在化学文献中。

items.en: The adjective appears almost only in front of a noun naming a method, an apparatus, a record or a grade. Since the method now works on colourless substances, the colour element of the name is historical, and only the notion of banded separation survives in figurative use.
items.cn: 这个形容词几乎只出现在表示方法、装置、记录或纯度的名词之前。由于该方法如今处理的是无色物质，名称中的颜色成分已成历史，只有「分层分离」的观念在比喻用法中留存。

items.en: First date uncertain: the adjective is recorded from the early twentieth century onward, but no single first citation is agreed, and any earlier date offered would be a guess.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：该形容词自二十世纪初起有记录，但没有公认的唯一最早书证，凡给出更早年代者均属推测。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look close to the adjective but come from other roots; group two holds terms for neighbouring laboratory methods.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但词根不同的词；第二组是实验室里相邻的其他分析方法。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek noun for colour, but with no writing element: it means 'of colour' in music and optics, not 'of the separation method'.
entries.definitionCN: 同样建立在希腊语「颜色」名词上，但不含「书写」成分：在音乐与光学中指「色彩的」，与分离方法无关。

entries.definition: A strand of a duplicated chromosome; the element here goes back to chromatin, and the resemblance to the colour noun is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制后染色体的一条；这里的成分源自染色质，与颜色名词的相似是偶然的。

entries.definition: From the Greek verb for writing, with no colour element: it means 'of drawing or visual presentation'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语表示书写的动词，不含颜色成分：意为「绘图的、视觉呈现的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the machine that performs the separation; it differs from the adjective only by the final element, and the two are often confused in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行分离的机器；它与形容词只差词尾成分，快速阅读时二者常被混淆。

entries.definition: Describes a separation driven by an electric field rather than by differential flow through a medium.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由电场驱动、而非靠流经介质的速度差实现的分离。

entries.definition: Describes the reading of a spectrum to identify substances; it analyses what is already mixed instead of splitting it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述通过读光谱来鉴定物质；它分析已经混在一起的东西，而不去拆分。

entries.definition: A general adjective for any method that determines what a sample contains; the chromatographic method is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何测定样品成分的方法，色谱法只是这一类中的一员。

entries.definition: Describes separation by spinning a sample so that heavier parts move outward; it sorts by mass, not by affinity for a medium.
entries.definitionCN: 描述靠旋转样品使较重部分外移的分离；它按质量分拣，而不是按对介质的亲和性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name joins a Greek noun for colour to a Greek verb for writing, so the technique is literally 'colour writing'.
normal.cn: 名称把希腊语的「颜色」名词与「书写」动词接在一起，这门技术字面上就是「颜色书写」。

normal.en: The family runs from the method to the machine to the picture: chromatography, chromatograph, chromatogram, chromatographic.
normal.cn: 同族词从方法到机器再到图像依次展开：表示方法的名词、表示仪器的名词、表示图谱的名词、以及这个形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: chromatographic separation, chromatographic column, chromatographic peak.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：色谱分离、色谱柱、色谱峰。

normal.en: A single run leaves a profile of peaks, which is why the adjective also names the record rather than only the method.
normal.cn: 一次进样会留下峰形轮廓，因此这个形容词也用来修饰记录，而不只修饰方法。

normal.en: The method sorts by how fast each component travels, so speed difference is the whole trick.
normal.cn: 该方法按各组分移动的快慢来分拣，速度差就是全部诀窍。

abstract.en: Picture a race in which every runner is timed and the results are written out as lines of different length.
abstract.cn: 想象一场比赛，每位选手都被计时，成绩被写成长短不一的横线。

abstract.en: Picture a choir splitting into sections by voice, each section standing in its own row.
abstract.cn: 想象一支合唱团按声部分开，每个声部各站成一排。

abstract.en: Picture a letter written in invisible ink that only shows its separate colours when warmed.
abstract.cn: 想象一封用隐形墨水写的信，加热后才显出各自分开的颜色。

examples.en: The chromatographic run cleanly separated the two isomers.
examples.cn: 这次色谱分离把两种异构体干净地分开了。

examples.en: Air samples were checked by a chromatographic method sensitive to traces.
examples.cn: 空气样品用一种对痕量敏感的色谱方法检测。

examples.en: The chromatographic trace is stored as a series of peak heights.
examples.cn: 色谱曲线以一系列峰高的形式保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「颜色书写」：表示颜色的成分加表示书写的成分，就是把混合物写成一条条色带 → 色谱的

root: 希腊语 khrōma「颜色」+ graphein「书写」，字面为「颜色书写」，由二十世纪初的植物学家为新分离方法命名；颜色成分如今只是历史遗留，方法本身已用于无色物质。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle a single attributive role: the adjective names the method, then the result, the apparatus, the record, the visual signature, the purity grade, a figurative split, and finally the literal colour-writing name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个定语角色转：这个形容词先指方法，再指结果、装置、记录、视觉特征、纯度等级、比喻性的拆分，最后回到字面的「颜色书写」之名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of mixed liquid climbing up paper and coming apart into bands of different length.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴混合液沿纸面向上爬，分成几条长短不一的色带。

branches.en: Method and product: the adjective first names the technique, then whatever the technique yields.
branches.cn: 方法与产物：先指技术本身，再指技术所产出之物。

branches.en: Hardware and standard: a column is built for the method, and a solvent is purified to its demand.
branches.cn: 硬件与标准：色谱柱为该法而造，溶剂为该法的要求而纯化。

branches.en: The trace as picture: peaks on a chart and bands on wet paper are the same separation seen twice.
branches.cn: 记录即图像：图上的峰与湿纸上的带，是同一次分离的两次显形。

branches.en: The split without a lab: any tangle sorted into separable parts borrows the gesture.
branches.cn: 离开实验室的拆分：任何被分成可分开部分的乱局都借用了这个动作。

branches.en: The name read back: colour plus writing still shows through every later use.
branches.cn: 回读名称：颜色加书写仍透在后来每一层用法里。

intro.en: The adjective is built from a Greek noun, a Greek verb and two suffixes, and the same pieces build the whole technical family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊语名词、希腊语动词与两个后缀构成，同样的部件也构成整个技术词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies both halves of the name: khrōma for colour and graphein for writing; Latin contributes only the later New Latin coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 名称的两半都来自希腊语：一半是颜色，一半是书写；拉丁语只提供了后世的新拉丁造词。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun of method into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把方法名词变成形容词。

items.example: The element marks any word built on the writing root.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标记一切建立在书写词根上的词。

items.example: The colour element survives only in the history of the name.
items.exampleCN: 颜色成分只留在这个名称的历史里。

items.example: The writing element names the record left on the medium.
items.exampleCN: 书写成分指留在介质上的记录。

items.meaning: the technique of separating by differential travel
items.meaningCN: 按差速移动进行分离的技术
items.example: The noun is the base from which the adjective is formed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的构词基础。

items.meaning: the instrument that performs the separation
items.example: The instrument suffix replaces the abstract noun ending.
items.exampleCN: 仪器后缀替换了抽象名词词尾。

items.meaning: the recorded trace of a run
items.meaningCN: 一次进样留下的记录曲线
items.example: The record suffix names the written result.
items.exampleCN: 记录后缀指书写出来的结果。

items.meaning: of the method or its products
items.meaningCN: 属于该方法或其产物的
items.example: The adjective is the form used in front of a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是置于名词前的形式。

items.example: The adverb modifies a verb of separating or measuring.
items.exampleCN: 副词修饰分离或测量的动词。

latinEntries.structure: New Latin coinage (early 20th century), from Greek stems
latinEntries.meaningCN: 色谱法，字面为颜色书写

definition_zh: 实验室器材；实验室器具与装置的总称
definition_en: the tools, instruments, vessels and consumable supplies needed to carry out work in a laboratory
core_image: 一条长实验台上排开烧杯、试管、滴管与一台离心机，桌下堆着未拆封的手套和离心管盒
scene: 生物教室里，学生把烧杯、试管和滴管一排摆上实验台，又在桌角放下一台离心机，桌下还堆着未拆封的手套。The laboratory equipment for the water test filled two long benches.
sceneCN: 这里 laboratory equipment 指「实验室里成套使用的器具与装置」（第 1 个义项：实验室工作所需器材的总称）；句意为这次水质检测的实验室器材占满了两条长实验台。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、试管、滴管、离心机、手套盒。

pos.zh: 实验室器材；实验室器具与装置的总称（多作不可数）

forms.label: 复数（同形，不作复数标记）

senses.title: The whole stock of gear in a lab
senses.titleCN: 实验室全部器材的总称
senses.definition: the full set of tools and devices used to carry out laboratory work, taken as one mass
senses.definitionCN: 把实验室工作所用的工具与装置作为一个整体来看的总称
senses.example: The laboratory equipment for the water test filled two long benches.
senses.exampleCN: 这次水质检测的实验室器材占满了两条长实验台。
senses.why: The phrase names a category rather than a single object, so it works like a mass noun for everything a bench needs.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是一个类别而非单件物品，因此它像不可数名词一样涵盖一条实验台所需的全部东西。

senses.title: Glassware as a class
senses.definition: the glass vessels of a lab, such as beakers, flasks, tubes and pipettes
senses.definitionCN: 实验室里的玻璃容器，如烧杯、烧瓶、试管与移液管
senses.example: Most of the laboratory equipment in that cupboard is heat-resistant glassware.
senses.exampleCN: 那个柜子里的实验室器材大多是耐热玻璃器皿。
senses.why: Glass is the oldest and most familiar part of the stock, so it often stands for the whole in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃器皿是这套器材里最古老也最熟悉的部分，日常说法里常以它代指全体。

senses.title: Instruments and analysers
senses.definition: the powered or precision devices that measure, separate or analyse samples
senses.definitionCN: 对样品进行测量、分离或分析的电动或精密装置
senses.example: The new laboratory equipment includes a centrifuge and a spectrometer.
senses.exampleCN: 新到的实验室器材包括一台离心机和一台光谱仪。
senses.why: As labs grew mechanised, machines became the expensive core of the stock, and the phrase shifted toward them.
senses.whyCN: 随着实验室机械化，机器成了这套器材中昂贵的大件，短语的重心也随之偏向它们。

senses.title: Consumables and protection
senses.definition: the supplies that are used up or worn, such as gloves, tubes and reagents
senses.definitionCN: 会被用掉或磨损的用品，如手套、离心管与试剂
senses.example: Gloves and sample tubes are counted as laboratory equipment in the annual order.
senses.exampleCN: 手套与样品管在年度采购里被算作实验室器材。
senses.why: Budgets treat everything a bench burns through as equipment, because it must be bought again and again.
senses.whyCN: 预算把实验台消耗掉的一切都算作器材，因为它们必须反复采购。

senses.title: A matched kit for one procedure
senses.titleCN: 为一套流程配齐的成套器材
senses.definition: a set of items assembled to work together for a particular procedure
senses.definitionCN: 为某一特定流程组装起来、彼此配套的一组物件
senses.example: The soil-testing laboratory equipment came in one locked case.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤检测的实验室器材装在一只带锁的箱子里。
senses.why: The phrase can name a purposeful subset, not only the whole room: what one procedure needs, fitted together.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也可指有目的的一个子集，而不只是整间实验室：某一流程所需之物被配成一套。

senses.title: The institutional stock and its cost
senses.titleCN: 机构层面的装备与开支
senses.definition: the apparatus owned by an institution and the money and upkeep it requires
senses.definitionCN: 机构所拥有的器材以及维持它所需的经费与维护
senses.example: Cutting the laboratory equipment budget delayed three student projects.
senses.exampleCN: 削减实验室器材预算使三个学生项目延期。
senses.why: Once equipment is owned by a department it becomes a line in a budget, and the phrase takes on that administrative sense.
senses.whyCN: 器材一旦归某系所有，就成了预算里的一行，短语也就带上这层管理含义。

senses.title: A classroom set for teaching
senses.titleCN: 课堂演示与教学用的一套器材
senses.definition: the simplified set of apparatus provided for students to perform set exercises
senses.definitionCN: 供学生完成规定练习使用的简化器材组合
senses.example: The school bought laboratory equipment sturdy enough for first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采购的实验室器材结实得足以让一年级学生使用。
senses.why: Teaching sets are chosen for safety and repetition rather than precision, which makes them a distinct kind of stock.
senses.whyCN: 教学套件按安全与耐用挑选，而非按精度，因此构成一类不同的器材。

senses.title: A researcher's working kit
senses.titleCN: 研究者的方法储备（比喻）
senses.definition: used figuratively for the set of methods and tools a researcher has learned to rely on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻研究者已经学会依赖的一整套方法与工具
senses.example: Statistical modelling became part of her laboratory equipment long before she had a lab.
senses.exampleCN: 早在拥有实验室之前，统计建模就已成了她的「实验器材」。
senses.why: The abstract use treats trained methods as instruments that one carries into any problem.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把训练有素的方法当作可以带进任何问题的器械。

intro.en: Two words meet in this phrase. The first goes back to Latin laborare 'to work'; the second goes back through French to a Norse verb for fitting out a ship. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个词合成。前者可追溯到拉丁语表示「劳作」的动词；后者经法语追溯到诺斯语中表示「装备船只」的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Laborare 'to work, toil' came from labor 'work, effort'. The deeper origin of labor is not established, and suggestions linking it to a verb meaning 'to totter' are hypotheses only.
items.cn: laborare 意为「劳作、辛劳」，来自 labor「劳动、辛苦」。labor 的更深来源未得到证明，把它与某个意为「摇晃」的动词相联系的看法只是假说。

items.en: A laboratorium was a place for work, and by the Middle Ages the word was applied specifically to the workshop of an alchemist or apothecary.
items.cn: laboratorium 本指干活的地方，到中世纪专指炼金术士或药剂师的作坊。

items.en: English adopted laboratory in the sixteenth century from the medieval Latin form; an older variant, elaboratory, was used for chemical workshops.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从中世纪拉丁形式吸收了这个词；更早的变体 elaboratory 曾用于指化学作坊。

items.en: The second word goes back to Old French esquiper 'to fit out a ship', from Old Norse skipa 'to arrange, equip a ship', related to skip 'ship'.
items.cn: 第二个词可追溯到古法语 esquiper「装备船只」，来自诺斯语 skipa「安排、装备船只」，与表示「船」的词相关。

items.en: In English equip first meant 'to furnish with what is needed'; equipment named the act of fitting out before it named the things provided.
items.cn: 在英语中，equip 最初意为「配备所需之物」；equipment 先指配备这一行为，后指被配备出来的东西。

items.en: The two words became a fixed phrase with the growth of institutional science in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. First date uncertain: the exact year the phrase became standard is not recorded.
items.cn: 随着十九、二十世纪机构化科学的发展，这两个词结合成固定短语。首见年代不确定：该短语成为通行说法的确切年份没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but belong to other roots; group two holds the ordinary terms for laboratory gear.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但词根不同的词；第二组是实验室器具的常用说法。

entries.definition: A room for washing, built on Latin lavare 'to wash'; it looks like laboratory but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指盥洗室，建立在拉丁语表示「洗」的动词上；外形像 laboratory，但与它没有共同词根。

entries.definition: An obsolete word for a chemical workshop; it looks like a longer form of laboratory but belonged to an older layer of usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学作坊的旧词；看起来像 laboratory 的更长形式，实则属于更早的用法层。

entries.definition: From the same ship-fitting verb, but it names a set of carriage horses or a retinue rather than laboratory gear.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「装备船只」的动词，但它指一套拉车的马或随从，而非实验室器具。

entries.definition: The verb means to furnish with what is needed; equipment is the resulting stock, so the two differ in word class only.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词意为配备所需之物；equipment 是配备出来的存量，两者只差词性。

entries.definition: A formal collective noun for the equipment of a particular activity, often suggesting a connected set of parts.
entries.definitionCN: 某一活动所用器材的正式集合名词，常暗示一套彼此相连的部件。

entries.definition: A single device made for measuring or doing something delicate; it is one member of the larger stock.
entries.definitionCN: 为测量或做精细工作而制的单件装置；它是整套器材中的一员。

entries.definition: The glass vessels of a lab taken as a class; it covers beakers and flasks but not machines.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类统称的实验室玻璃容器；涵盖烧杯与烧瓶，但不含机器。

entries.definition: The expendable goods a lab uses up, such as gloves and reagents; equipment can be kept, supplies cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室会用尽的消耗品，如手套与试剂；器材可以留存，耗材则不能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase splits into a place of work and a verb for fitting out, so it means the things a workplace is fitted out with.
normal.cn: 这个短语可拆成「劳作之地」与「配备」两部分，因此指一个工作场所被配备出来的那些东西。

normal.en: The second word began with ships: to equip was to fit out a vessel before it was to fit out a bench.
normal.cn: 第二个词最初与船有关：配备原指把一条船装备齐全，后来才用于实验台。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the administrative life of the stock: equipment list, equipment room, equipment budget.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这套器材的管理轨迹：器材清单、器材室、器材预算。

normal.en: The family runs equip, equipped, equipment, equipage, re-equip, all from the fitting-out verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括配备、已配备的、设备、成套用具、重新装备，都出自那个「装备」动词。

normal.en: A lab bench is read in layers: glass in front, instruments behind, consumables underneath.
normal.cn: 实验台可以分层来读：前排玻璃器皿，后排仪器，台下耗材。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's hold being packed for a long voyage, every item checked against a list.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船的货舱正为远航被打点，每件东西都对着清单核过。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen whose drawers were filled by someone who knew every recipe in advance.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，抽屉是被一个事先知道所有菜谱的人填满的。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller who carries a small case that opens into a whole workshop.
abstract.cn: 想象一位旅人带着一只小箱子，打开就是整间作坊。

examples.en: Every piece of laboratory equipment must be logged after use.
examples.cn: 每件实验室器材使用后都必须登记。

examples.en: The department replaced its old laboratory equipment with digital meters.
examples.cn: 该系用数字仪表替换了旧的实验室器材。

examples.en: Students learn to clean laboratory equipment before they run any test.
examples.cn: 学生在做任何检测之前先要学会清理实验室器材。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「干活的地方 + 配备」：为劳作之地配齐的一整套家当 → 实验室器材

root: laboratory 来自中世纪拉丁 laboratorium「干活的地方」，词根为拉丁 laborare「劳作」，labor 更深来源不确定；equipment 经古法语 esquiper「装备船只」上溯诺斯语 skipa，本义为把船配备齐全，后泛指配备出来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole stock of a lab to its glass, its machines, its consumables, a matched kit, an institutional budget line, a classroom set, and finally a researcher's trained methods.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实验室的全部器材，依次移到玻璃器皿、仪器、耗材、成套配件、机构预算项、课堂套件，最后到研究者训练有素的方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long bench loaded with glass, steel and boxes, everything a day's work requires.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长实验台，摆满玻璃、钢铁与盒子，一天工作所需的一切都在上面。

branches.en: Stock and ledger: the same mass of gear seen once on the bench and once in a budget.
branches.cn: 存量与账目：同一批器材，一次看在实验台上，一次看在预算里。

branches.en: Two materials of the bench: vessels of glass in front, instruments of steel behind.
branches.cn: 实验台的两种材料：前排玻璃器皿，后排钢铁仪器。

branches.en: What is used up and what is fitted together: gloves vanish, a test kit stays assembled.
branches.cn: 用尽之物与配好之物：手套会用完，检测套件则保持成套。

branches.en: The teaching version: the same stock simplified for young hands and repeated lessons.
branches.cn: 教学版本：同一套器材为年轻的手与反复的课而简化。

branches.en: The kit one carries: methods become instruments that travel with the researcher.
branches.cn: 随身的那套：方法成了随研究者移动的器械。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are built from ordinary morphemes, and each half also supports a small family of English words.
intro.cn: 短语的两半都由寻常语素构成，每一半还各自支撑一小族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin laborare and laboratorium stand behind the first word; the second comes from French and Norse rather than Latin, so the phrase mixes two lineages.
latinIntro.cn: 第一个词背后是拉丁语的劳作动词与工作场所名词；第二个词来自法语与诺斯语而非拉丁语，因此这个短语混合了两条血脉。

items.example: The laboratory is where the stock is kept.
items.exampleCN: 实验室就是这套器材存放的地方。

items.example: The first word begins with the idea of work itself.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词从「劳作」这一观念开始。

items.meaning: a place where something is done
items.example: The suffix turns a verb of working into a name for the workplace.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「劳作」动词变成工作场所之名。

items.structure: Old French esquiper, from Old Norse skipa
items.example: To equip a bench is the same gesture as fitting out a ship.
items.exampleCN: 装备一张实验台，与把一条船配备齐全，是同一个动作。

items.meaning: the things provided for an activity
items.meaningCN: 为某项活动提供的东西
items.example: The noun turns the act of fitting out into the stock itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把配备的行为转为配备出来的存量。

items.example: A well-equipped lab is one whose stock is complete.
items.exampleCN: 装备良好的实验室，就是器材齐备的实验室。

items.example: Old benches are re-equipped rather than replaced.
items.exampleCN: 旧实验台是重新装备，而不是整台换掉。

items.example: The fixed phrase joins the place to what fills it.
items.exampleCN: 这个固定短语把场所与填满它的东西接在一起。

items.meaning: describing a room, list or budget for such gear
items.meaningCN: 描述器材室、清单或预算的
items.example: The hyphenated form works as a modifier before another noun.
items.exampleCN: 带连字符的形式在另一名词前作修饰语。

derivatives.zh: 成套用具；车马随从（旧式）

definition_en: a test carried out under controlled conditions to discover or check something; also to carry out such a test, or to try something new
core_image: 两只同样的杯子并排放着，一只加了糖，一只没有，旁边一张纸上只写着一个待验证的问题
scene: 厨房桌上并排放着两只同样的杯子，一只加了糖，一只没加，旁边摊着一张写着待验证问题的纸。The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
sceneCN: 这里 experiment 指「在受控条件下检验某个设想的实验」（第 1 个义项：受控的科学检验）；句意为这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。图中可辨识物件：两只杯子、糖罐、记录纸、铅笔。

pos.zh: 实验；试验；（新事物的）尝试

senses.title: A controlled scientific test
senses.definition: a procedure carried out under controlled conditions in order to test a hypothesis or discover a fact
senses.definitionCN: 为检验假设或发现事实而在受控条件下进行的操作
senses.example: The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
senses.exampleCN: 这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。
senses.why: The core sense is a deliberate trial in which conditions are arranged so that one factor can be watched.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是有意的试验：把条件安排好，好让某一个因素被观察。

senses.title: A tentative attempt
senses.definition: an attempt made without assurance of success, in order to learn what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在并无成功把握的情况下做出尝试，只为看看会怎样
senses.example: Her first attempt at repairing the radio was an experiment rather than a repair.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次修收音机，更像一次试验，而不是一次修理。
senses.why: Outside science the word keeps the same shape without the controls: you try something because you do not yet know the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 在科学之外，这个词保留了同样的形态，只是没有受控条件：你因为还不知道结果而去试一试。

senses.title: A set exercise in a teaching lab
senses.titleCN: 课堂上按规程做的实验
senses.definition: a prescribed practical exercise that students perform to see a known result for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 学生按既定规程操作、亲眼看到已知结果的一种练习
senses.example: The class does the same experiment with vinegar and baking soda every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班每年秋天都做同一个醋与小苏打的实验。
senses.why: School labs repeat experiments whose answers are already known, so the word comes to mean the exercise rather than the inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 学校实验室重复的是答案已知的实验，于是这个词转而指那道练习，而非那次探究。

senses.title: A thought experiment
senses.definition: a scenario imagined in detail in order to test a principle that cannot be tried in reality
senses.definitionCN: 为检验无法在现实中操作的原理想象出来的详细情境
senses.example: Einstein's experiment with a falling elevator was carried out only in his head.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦那个关于下落电梯的实验只在头脑中进行。
senses.why: When the apparatus is imagination, the trial still keeps the name, because the point is still to test an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当器械换成想象时，这种试仍然沿用旧名，因为要点依旧是检验一个想法。

senses.title: An innovative departure
senses.titleCN: 在艺术或政策上的一次新尝试
senses.definition: a new way of doing something, tried in order to see whether it works better
senses.definitionCN: 为看清是否更好而尝试的一种新做法
senses.example: The theatre's experiment with a bare stage divided its critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院对空舞台的尝试使评论界分成两派。
senses.why: Any field that risks a new form borrows the word, since the new form is staked on an unknown outcome.
senses.whyCN: 任何冒险采用新形式的领域都会借用这个词，因为新形式押在一个未知的结果上。

senses.title: To carry out a scientific test
senses.definition: to perform a controlled test in order to gather evidence
senses.definitionCN: 为收集证据而进行受控检验
senses.example: They experimented on the alloy until they found its breaking point.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这种合金反复做实验，直到找出它的断裂点。
senses.why: The verb is simply the activity named by the noun, turned into something one does.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词所指的活动，转成一个人去做的事情。

senses.title: To try something out
senses.definition: to try a substance, method or style in order to learn its effects
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清效果而试用某种物质、方法或风格
senses.example: He experimented with colder water and the tea stopped tasting bitter.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着用更冷的水，茶就不再发苦了。
senses.why: The verb broadens from the laboratory to any deliberate trial of a variable.
senses.whyCN: 动词从实验室扩展开来，指对某一变量做的任何有意的试用。

senses.title: A venture in one's own life
senses.titleCN: 人生中的一次尝试（抽象义）
senses.definition: used of a period or venture in which someone tries a different way of living or working
senses.definitionCN: 指某人尝试另一种生活或工作方式的一段时期或一项事业
senses.example: Moving to the coast was an experiment in living more slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到海边，是一次把日子过慢些的尝试。
senses.why: The abstract sense treats a life choice as a trial whose result cannot be known in advance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把人生选择当作一场结果无法预知的试验。

intro.en: Experiment goes back to Latin experiri 'to try, test', whose noun experimentum meant 'a trial, a proof'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 experiri「尝试、检验」，其名词 experimentum 意为「试、证明」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Periri meant 'to try, to attempt', and from the same stock came periculum 'trial, danger' and peritus 'experienced'. The link among them is generally accepted.
items.cn: periri 意为「尝试、试探」，同一词干还生出 periculum「试、危险」与 peritus「有经验的」。三者之间的关联一般认为是可靠的。

items.en: The prefix ex- 'out' added to periri gave experiri 'to try out, to test thoroughly', with the sense of carrying a trial through to its end.
items.cn: 前缀 ex-「向外」加 periri 构成 experiri「试出来、彻底检验」，带有把试验做到尽头的意思。

items.en: The noun experimentum named a trial, a proof or a piece of evidence, and also the experience gained from trying.
items.cn: 名词 experimentum 指一次试验、一项证明或一份证据，也指由尝试得来的经验。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century through French, at first with the older sense of experience or observation rather than a staged procedure.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经法语吸收这个词，最初取的是「经验、观察」的旧义，而非安排好的操作步骤。

items.en: From the seventeenth century, with the rise of organised investigation, the word settled into its present meaning of a controlled test of a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，随着有组织的探究兴起，这个词固定为今天「对假设作受控检验」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin form): the root behind periri is reconstructed, and though the family with peril and expert is widely accepted, no attested earlier form can be quoted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前的形态）：periri 背后的词根属重构形式；尽管它与表示危险、有经验的同族关系被广泛接受，却没有可引用的更早实证形式。

note.en: Group one separates the near relatives built on the same Latin root; group two separates the ordinary words for a test.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同出拉丁词根的近亲；第二组辨析表示「检验」的常用词。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb for trying, but it means what one has lived through, not a staged test.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个表示尝试的动词，但指亲身经历过的事，而非安排好的检验。

entries.definition: From the adjective for 'experienced', so an expert is one who has tried things and learned; it names a person, not a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「有经验的」形容词，因此指试过并学到东西的人；它指人，不指程序。

entries.definition: From the noun for a trial that puts one at risk, so it survives only as the word for serious danger.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示带风险的试的名词，因此只留下「严重危险」这一义。

entries.definition: The doer of an experiment; the difference from the noun is only the agent suffix, which is easy to miss in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指做实验的人；与名词的差别只在表示施动者的后缀，快速阅读时容易看漏。

entries.definition: The general word for checking whether something works or is true; an experiment is its formal, scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指检查某物是否有效或属实的词；experiment 是它正式、科学化的对应词。

entries.definition: A trial is a first use or run to see how something performs, often of a product or a method already made.
entries.definitionCN: 指为看某物表现如何而作的首次使用或试运行，多用于已经做成的产品或方法。

entries.definition: A study is a planned investigation, often longer and observational; not every study manipulates conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指有计划的调查，通常更长且偏观察；并非每项研究都操纵条件。

entries.definition: To probe is to investigate something hidden or unclear, often with repeated small inquiries rather than one designed trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指追查隐藏或不明之事，常用反复的小探询，而非一次设计好的试验。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is built from a Latin verb for trying plus a prefix meaning 'out', so it is a trying-out to the end.
normal.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「尝试」的动词加一个意为「向外」的前缀构成，因此是「试到底」。

normal.en: The same root gives peril and expert: a trial is risky, and one who has come through trials is experienced.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出「危险」与「有经验的」：试是有风险的，闯过许多试的人便有经验。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: carry out an experiment, a controlled experiment, experiment with a new method.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法：进行实验、对照实验、尝试新方法。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one form, so the thing and the doing are the same word.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，因此这件事与做这件事是同一个词。

normal.en: A thought experiment keeps the name even when the apparatus is only imagination.
normal.cn: 思想实验即使器械只是想象，也仍沿用这个名字。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cups on a table, differing in exactly one spoonful.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只一模一样的杯子，只差一勺东西。

abstract.en: Picture a lock with many keys, tried one at a time while someone writes down each result.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁与许多钥匙，一把一把地试，旁边有人记下每次结果。

abstract.en: Picture a life lived for one year as a question rather than an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象把一年生活当作一个问题来过，而不是当作一个答案。

examples.en: The experiment showed that the plants grew faster in weak light.
examples.cn: 实验显示这些植物在弱光下长得更快。

examples.en: She experimented with three glazes before choosing one.
examples.cn: 她试了三种釉料才选定一种。

examples.en: No experiment on human subjects was allowed without consent.
examples.cn: 未经同意不得在人类受试者身上做实验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「试到底」：前缀表示向外，词根表示尝试，把一件事一直试到见结果 → 实验、尝试

root: 拉丁 experiri「尝试、检验」= ex-「向外」+ periri「试」；同族有 periculum「危险」与 peritus「有经验的」；experiri 的拉丁语之前形态属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture, a deliberate trial: first the controlled test, then any tentative attempt, a classroom exercise, a trial run only in the mind, a new departure, the act of testing, trying a variable, and finally a life tried as an experiment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开，即有意的一次试：先是在受控条件下的检验，接着是任何试探性的尝试、课堂练习、只在头脑中进行的试、一种新做法、做实验这一行为、试用某个变量，最后把人生本身当作一次试验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cups differing by one spoonful, and a written question waiting for an answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只只差一勺的相同杯子，以及一个等着答案的书面问题。

branches.en: The designed trial and the act of running it: the noun and the verb name one operation.
branches.cn: 设计好的试与执行这次试：名词与动词指同一操作。

branches.en: The loose attempt: trying something without guarantees, whether a repair or a colder cup of tea.
branches.cn: 宽松的试：在没有保证的情况下试，无论是修东西还是换冷水泡茶。

branches.en: The exercise and the imagined run: both repeat a known or imagined procedure for the sake of seeing.
branches.cn: 练习与想象中的试：两者都为「看见」而重演一个已知或设想的过程。

branches.en: The departure: a new form staked on an unknown outcome, in theatre or in policy.
branches.cn: 新做法：把新形式押在未知结果上，无论在剧场还是在政策上。

branches.en: The life trial: a year lived as a question rather than an answer.
branches.cn: 人生的试：把一年当作问题而非答案来过。

intro.en: Experiment is a Latin verb-noun pair in which a prefix, a root and a suffix each carry part of the meaning, and the same pieces build its English family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一组拉丁动词与名词，前缀、词根与后缀各担一部分意义，同样的部件也构成它的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin periri and its noun periculum supply the root; ex- adds the sense of carrying a trial through, and -mentum names the result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「试」的动词与其名词提供词根；前缀增添「把试做到底」的意思，后缀则命名结果。

items.example: The prefix makes the trying exhaustive rather than casual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「试」成为彻底的，而非随意的。

items.example: The root carries the whole idea of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「试」的全部意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the record or result of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词转为一次试的记录或结果。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The Latin noun already joins the act and its evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已把行为与其证据合在一起。

items.example: English keeps one form for the thing and the doing.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个形式兼指这件事与做这件事。

items.example: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the testing stage.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记属于试验阶段的一切。

items.example: The noun names the practice rather than one trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指实践，而非某一次试。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person running the trial.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指执行这次试的人。

definition_zh: 数学；数学学科；（某事物的）数学计算部分
definition_en: the branch of study that deals with numbers, quantities, shapes and the relations between them, using logical reasoning
core_image: 一整面黑板上密密的算式，粉笔灰落在槽沿，最后一行的等号被重重描了一遍
scene: 教室里一整面黑板写满算式，一名学生在角落补上一个等号，粉笔灰落在槽沿。She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematics 指「作为一门学科的数学」（第 1 个义项：研究数与形及其关系的学问）；句意为她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。图中可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、算式、板槽。

pos.zh: 数学（学科名，形式为复数而作单数用）

senses.title: The discipline as a whole
senses.definition: the field of study that reasons about number, quantity, structure and shape
senses.definitionCN: 研究数、量、结构与形的学问领域
senses.example: She studied mathematics for four years before turning to economics.
senses.exampleCN: 她学了四年数学之后才转向经济学。
senses.why: The word names a whole discipline rather than one of its branches, so it is used with a singular verb despite its plural shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整门学问而非某一分支，因此尽管外形是复数，却接单数动词。

senses.title: The school subject and its lessons
senses.definition: the subject taught in schools, together with the lessons and examinations that go with it
senses.definitionCN: 学校里教授的这一科目，以及随之而来的课程与考试
senses.example: Mathematics is timetabled before lunch three days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 数学课每周有三天排在午饭前。
senses.why: Once a discipline enters a timetable it becomes a subject, and the same word covers both the field and the hour it occupies.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问一旦进入课表就成了科目，同一个词既指这个领域，也指它占用的那一节课。

senses.title: Reckoning and reasoning in practice
senses.titleCN: 实际推算与推理的活动
senses.definition: the activity of calculating and reasoning with numbers in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情境中运用数字进行计算与推理的活动
senses.example: The mathematics behind the bridge design was checked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥设计背后的数学计算被核对了两遍。
senses.why: Here the word means the working itself, not the science of it: the sums someone actually did.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指实际运算本身，而不是关于运算的学问：某人真做过的那些计算。

senses.title: The mathematical side of a subject
senses.titleCN: 某一对象内部的数学机制
senses.definition: the quantitative structure and relationships that underlie a particular process or system
senses.definitionCN: 支撑某一过程或系统的数量结构与关系
senses.example: The mathematics of traffic flow decides where queues form.
senses.exampleCN: 车流的数学机制决定了排队会在哪里形成。
senses.why: Any system with regular quantities has a mathematics of its own, and the phrase names that structure rather than the discipline.
senses.whyCN: 任何具有规律数量的系统都有自己的数学，这个说法指那套结构，而非那门学科。

senses.title: The professional community
senses.definition: the community of people who work in the field, taken as a body
senses.definitionCN: 以整体看待的、从事这一领域的人所组成的群体
senses.example: The result was celebrated across mathematics before it was published.
senses.exampleCN: 这一结果在发表之前就已在数学界传开。
senses.why: A discipline also names its practitioners as a group, which is why one can speak of a whole field being excited.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问也指其从业者的群体，因此可以说整个领域为之振奋。

senses.title: Careful reckoning in plain speech
senses.definition: used informally for the calculating needed to make a decision come out right
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指为使某项决定算得过来所需的精密推算
senses.example: The mathematics of the deal did not survive the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易的账在新税之下算不过来了。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the discipline's name for the arithmetic of a practical decision.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法借这门学问之名，指一项实际决定背后的加减账。

senses.title: The old sense of learning
senses.definition: in its Greek origin, any branch of learning rather than the numerical sciences alone
senses.definitionCN: 在其希腊来源中泛指任何一门学问，而非仅指数理科学
senses.example: In the ancient curriculum, music and astronomy counted as mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 在古代课程里，音乐与天文也算作数学。
senses.why: The Greek word meant something learned, so the discipline once covered far more ground than it does now.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词意为「被学到的东西」，因此这门学问早先涵盖的范围远大于今天。

senses.title: The mathematical content of a paper
senses.titleCN: 论文或模型中的数学内容
senses.definition: the equations, proofs and derivations contained in a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 一项工作中所含的方程、证明与推导
senses.example: The biology paper was strong, but its mathematics was thin.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇生物学论文很强，但其中的数学部分薄弱。
senses.why: Readers separate a work's subject matter from its mathematical machinery, and this sense names the latter.
senses.whyCN: 读者会把一项工作的主题与其数学工具分开，这个义项指后者。

intro.en: The word goes back to Greek mathēma 'that which is learned', from manthanein 'to learn'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到希腊语 mathēma「被学到的东西」，源自动词 manthanein「学习」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Manthanein meant 'to learn', and gave mathēma 'a lesson, something learned' and mathesis 'learning'. The deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: manthanein 意为「学习」，由此得到 mathēma「课业、所学之物」与 mathesis「学习」。更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Mathēmatikos meant 'fond of learning, learned'; ta mathēmatika named the things studied rather than a single science.
items.cn: mathēmatikos 意为「爱学习的、有学问的」；中性复数形式指的是所学的那些东西，而非单一学科。

items.en: The phrase mathēmatikē tekhnē, 'the art of learning', was narrowed by Plato and Aristotle to arithmetic, geometry, astronomy and music.
items.cn: 「学习的技艺」这一短语经柏拉图与亚里士多德之手，收窄为算术、几何、天文与音乐四门。

items.en: Latin took mathematica as a name for that group of studies, and medieval schools taught them in the quadrivial curriculum.
items.cn: 拉丁语以 mathematica 作为这组学问之名，中世纪学校在四艺课程中教授它们。

items.en: English adopted the word in the sixteenth century; the plural form is treated as singular because it names one field.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词；复数外形被当作单数使用，因为它命名的是一个领域。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the field expanded far beyond number and shape, and the old sense of any learning survives only in histories of the curriculum. First date uncertain: the earliest English citation is placed in the sixteenth century but no single year is agreed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，该领域远远超出数与形，而「任何学问」的旧义只留在课程史中。首见年代不确定：最早英语书证被放在十六世纪，但没有公认的确切年份。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the same word that are easy to mix up; group two separates the neighbouring branches of the field.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同一个词的各种形式，第二组辨析相邻的学科分支。

entries.definition: An older singular and adjective form, now rare; modern English keeps the plural shape for the field and uses mathematical for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的单数形式与形容词形式，今已罕用；现代英语以复数外形指该领域，形容词则另用形式。

entries.definition: The adjective of the field; it describes work or reasoning rather than naming the discipline itself.
entries.definitionCN: 该领域的形容词；它描述工作或推理，而不命名学科本身。

entries.definition: The practitioner; the ending marks a person, which is the one clear difference from the field name.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；词尾标记出人，这是与学科名唯一清楚的差别。

entries.definition: A rare English borrowing of the Greek noun for learning, used in older philosophical writing; it never named the school subject.
entries.definitionCN: 英语直接从希腊语借入的罕见名词，意为学习，见于较早的哲学写作；它从未指学校科目。

entries.definition: The branch that handles counting and the four operations; it is a part of mathematics, not a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 处理计数与四则运算的分支；它是数学的一部分，而不是数学的同义词。

entries.definition: The branch that works with symbols standing for unknown numbers; one department within the larger field.
entries.definitionCN: 用符号代表未知数进行运算的分支；是更大领域中的一个部门。

entries.definition: The branch that studies shape, size and the relations of figures in space.
entries.definitionCN: 研究形状、大小与空间中图形关系的分支。

entries.definition: The practical ability to handle numbers in daily life; it is a skill, whereas mathematics is a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 在日常生活中处理数字的实际能力；它是一种技能，而数学是一门学问。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Greek root means 'that which is learned', so mathematics began as the name for any studied subject.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「被学到的东西」，因此数学最初泛指任何被研习的科目。

normal.en: The plural shape takes a singular verb: mathematics is one field, not many.
normal.cn: 复数外形接单数动词：数学是一个领域，而不是许多个。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the division of the field: pure mathematics, applied mathematics, advanced mathematics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域的划分：纯数学、应用数学、高等数学。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the clippings math and maths.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有口语缩略形式。

normal.en: Ancient schooling grouped it with music and astronomy, so the old sense was wider than today's.
normal.cn: 古代课程把它与音乐、天文编在一起，因此旧义比今天宽。

abstract.en: Picture a single chalk line drawn again and again until it is unmistakably straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条粉笔线被反复描画，直到直得无可置疑。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens every locked door in a building, whatever the door was made for.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙能打开楼里每一扇锁着的门，无论那扇门原本是做什么用的。

abstract.en: Picture a language spoken by few people but understood, in translation, by everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象一种只有少数人会说的语言，却人人能通过翻译读懂。

examples.en: Mathematics is compulsory for every student in the first two years.
examples.cn: 头两年每个学生都必须学数学。

examples.en: The mathematics of the model turned out to be simpler than expected.
examples.cn: 这个模型的数学部分比预想的简单。

examples.en: He teaches mathematics at a secondary school.
examples.cn: 他在一所中学教数学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学来的东西」：希腊词根意为学习，凡学得的学问都算 → 数学

root: 希腊 mathēma「被学到的东西」源自动词 manthanein「学习」，mathēmatikē tekhnē 经柏拉图与亚里士多德收窄为四艺；拉丁 mathematica 承之，英语十六世纪借入，复数外形作单数用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline as a whole to its school hours, its practical working, the structure inside another subject, its professional community, plain-speech reckoning, the ancient sense of any learning, and the mathematics inside a single paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从作为整体的学科，移到它的课时、实际运算、另一对象内部的结构、专业共同体、口语里的算账、古代泛指学问的旧义，最后到一篇论文里的数学部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blackboard filled with lines of symbols, one equal sign pressed hard at the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满符号行的黑板，末尾一个被重重描过的等号。

branches.en: The field and its old name: what began as any studied subject became one discipline.
branches.cn: 领域与其旧名：最初泛指任何被研习的科目，后来成了一口学科。

branches.en: Where it is taught and where it is printed: a timetable hour and a thin section of a paper.
branches.cn: 教它的地方与印它的地方：课表上的一节，论文里薄弱的一节。

branches.en: Reckoning in practice: the sums behind a bridge or behind a deal.
branches.cn: 实际算账：桥背后的算式，或一笔交易背后的账。

branches.en: The hidden structure: every regular system carries a mathematics of its own.
branches.cn: 隐在的结构：每个有规律的系统都自带一套数学。

branches.en: The people: a field is also the body of those who work in it.
branches.cn: 人：一个领域也是从事者的群体。

intro.en: The English word is a Greek noun with a Greek suffix, filtered through Latin and given an English plural ending.
intro.cn: 这个英语词是一个希腊名词加希腊后缀，经拉丁语过滤，又换上英语复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma and mathēmatikos supply the meaning; Latin mathematica fixed the school subject, and English added the plural -s.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语的名词与形容词提供意义；拉丁语固定了学科之名，英语再加复数词尾。

items.example: The root names learning before it names number.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根先指学习，后指数。

items.example: The verb stands at the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词位于整个词族的起点。

items.example: The suffix names a skilled practice, not a body of facts.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门技艺，而非一堆事实。

items.meaningCN: 有学问的；属于数学之物的
items.example: The adjective shifted from 'learned' to 'numerical'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「有学问的」转为「数理的」。

items.example: Latin fixed the plural shape that English inherited.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语固定了英语所继承的复数外形。

items.structure: English plural ending used for fields of study
items.example: The ending marks a discipline while keeping a plural look.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记一门学科，同时保留复数外形。

items.example: The word names one field with a plural form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词以复数形式命名一个领域。

items.example: The adjective serves whenever a noun follows.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于修饰后面的名词。

items.meaning: a person who works in the field
items.example: The person suffix completes the family.
items.exampleCN: 表人后缀补全了词族。

latinEntries.structure: mathesis, mathesis (f., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 数学的；数学方法的；精确严密的
definition_en: relating to mathematics or to its methods; also used of reasoning that is as exact as mathematics
core_image: 一张草稿纸上，几行推导被框起来，旁边用箭头标出「若此，则彼」的关系
scene: 桌上摊着一张草稿纸，几行推导被方框圈住，旁边用箭头标出从前提到结论的去向。The proof rests on a purely mathematical argument, with no measurement involved.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematical 指「属于数学本身的」（第 1 个义项：与数学学科相关）；句意为这个证明依靠纯数学论证，不涉及任何测量。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、方框、箭头、铅笔。

pos.zh: 数学的；数学方法的；精确严密的

senses.title: Belonging to mathematics
senses.definition: relating to the discipline of mathematics as such
senses.definitionCN: 与数学这门学科本身有关
senses.example: The proof rests on a purely mathematical argument, with no measurement involved.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明依靠纯数学论证，不涉及任何测量。
senses.why: The plainest reading simply attaches the discipline's name to the thing described.
senses.whyCN: 最朴素的用法只是把学科之名挂到所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Using the tools of mathematics
senses.titleCN: 使用数学工具与方法的
senses.definition: carried out by means of equations, symbols or formal derivation
senses.definitionCN: 借助方程、符号或形式推导来完成的
senses.example: The paper gives a mathematical treatment of the spread of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文用数学方法处理疾病的传播。
senses.why: When a problem is handled with symbols rather than observations, the adjective marks the instrument used.
senses.whyCN: 当一个问题靠符号而非观察来处理时，这个形容词标出的就是所用工具。

senses.title: Exact and rigorously reasoned
senses.titleCN: 精确而推理严密的（引申）
senses.definition: so exact and tightly reasoned that no step is left loose
senses.definitionCN: 精确且推理严密，以致没有任何一步是松的
senses.example: Her account of the meeting was mathematical in its precision.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那次会议的叙述精确得像数学。
senses.why: Mathematics is the model of step-by-step certainty, so the adjective lends that quality to anything else.
senses.whyCN: 数学是一步接一步确定性的典范，这个形容词便把这种品质借给别的对象。

senses.title: Good with numbers
senses.definition: having a natural or trained ability with numbers and reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在数字与推理上有天赋或受过训练的
senses.example: He is the most mathematical of the three children.
senses.exampleCN: 三个孩子里他最有数学头脑。
senses.why: A person can carry the adjective because ability in the field is a property of people.
senses.whyCN: 人可以带这个形容词，因为该领域的能力是人的属性。

senses.title: Abstract and symbol-driven
senses.definition: described as abstract, symbolic and detached from concrete objects
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为抽象的、符号化的、与具体事物脱开的
senses.example: The objection was too mathematical to satisfy the historians.
senses.exampleCN: 这个反对意见过于数学化，历史学家无法接受。
senses.why: To call something mathematical can also criticise it as remote from lived detail.
senses.whyCN: 说某物「太数学」也可以是在批评它远离实际细节。

senses.title: Treatable by a model
senses.definition: capable of being described and predicted by equations
senses.definitionCN: 能够用方程来描述和预测的
senses.example: Once the system became mathematical, its future could be simulated.
senses.exampleCN: 这个系统一旦被数学化，它的未来就可以模拟。
senses.why: A messy process becomes mathematical when it is reduced to quantities a model can carry.
senses.whyCN: 混乱的过程一旦被化简为模型能承载的量，就变得「可数学处理」。

senses.title: Of a formal proof
senses.definition: established by deductive proof from stated assumptions rather than by experiment
senses.definitionCN: 由所述前提演绎证明、而非由实验确立的
senses.example: No experiment can settle a question that is mathematical in form.
senses.exampleCN: 形式上属于数学的问题，任何实验都无法解决。
senses.why: Proof is the field's own way of settling things, so the adjective names that kind of certainty.
senses.whyCN: 证明是这门学问自己的定案方式，这个形容词便命名那种确定性。

senses.title: As certain as arithmetic
senses.titleCN: 像算术一样确定无疑的
senses.definition: used hyperbolically of a conclusion that seems impossible to dispute
senses.definitionCN: 夸张地用于形容似乎无可争辩的结论
senses.example: The failure was mathematical: given those prices, the firm could not survive.
senses.exampleCN: 这次失败是算定的：在那些价格下，公司无法存活。
senses.why: The hyperbolic use treats an outcome as something already written into the numbers.
senses.whyCN: 夸张用法把某个结果当作早已写进数字里的东西。

intro.en: The adjective is the Greek adjective for 'learned' or 'mathematical', plus the Latin adjectival ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊语表示「有学问的、数学的」形容词加拉丁形容词词尾构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mathēma 'something learned, a lesson' came from manthanein 'to learn'; the root behind the verb is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: mathēma「所学之物、课业」源自动词 manthanein「学习」；动词背后的词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Mathēmatikos 'fond of learning, learned' was formed with the suffix -ikos 'belonging to'; it described people and things alike.
items.cn: mathēmatikos「爱学习、有学问的」由表示「属于」的后缀构成；人与物都可用它描述。

items.en: The neuter plural named the mathematical studies, and this is the form Latin took over.
items.cn: 中性复数指数学诸科，拉丁语承接的正是这个形式。

items.en: Latin mathematicus served as both adjective and noun, and could also mean 'astrologer' in later use.
items.cn: 拉丁 mathematicus 兼作形容词与名词，在后世也可指「占星者」。

items.en: English added the adjectival ending to the Latin stem in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, alongside the noun mathematics.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪给拉丁词干加上形容词词尾，与名词 mathematics 并行。

items.en: The sense 'exact, rigorously reasoned' grew from the prestige of proof, and is now the most common figurative use. First date uncertain: no single year is recorded for this extension.
items.cn: 「精确、推理严密」义由证明的声望生长出来，如今是最常见的比喻用法。首见年代不确定：这一引申没有确切年份记录。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from its own family; group two separates words that also claim precision.
note.cn: 第一组辨析这个形容词与其同族形式；第二组辨析同样声称精确的词。

entries.definition: The older adjective and singular noun, now largely replaced by mathematical and mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的形容词与单数名词，今基本被「数学的」与「数学」两个形式取代。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the adjective differs from it only by its ending, which is easy to miss in a scan.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科本身；形容词与它只差词尾，快速扫读时容易看漏。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field; the ending marks a person where the adjective marks a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指该领域的从业者；词尾标出人，而形容词标出性质。

entries.definition: The adverb modifies a verb, as in 'mathematically trained'; it cannot stand before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 副词修饰动词，如「受过数学训练」；它不能置于名词前。

entries.definition: Concerned with numbers as such, often in the sense of values rather than proofs.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及数字本身，常指数值而非证明。

entries.definition: Concerned with measuring amounts; a quantitative study may use little formal mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及测量数量；定量研究可能只用很少的形式数学。

entries.definition: Strict and thorough in method; it praises careful procedure without invoking mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 方法上严格彻底；它称赞程序的严谨，却不必涉及数学。

entries.definition: Precise in measurement or statement; mathematical reasoning is exact, but an exact figure need not be proved.
entries.definitionCN: 在测量或表述上精确；数学推理是精确的，但一个精确数字未必经过证明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the discipline's name turned into a modifier, so it always describes something that belongs to the field.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是学科名转成的修饰语，因此总描述属于该领域之物。

normal.en: The Greek root meant 'learned', so the earliest sense praised learning rather than calculation.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「有学问的」，因此最早的义项称赞的是学问，而非计算。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: mathematical model, mathematical proof, mathematical notation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：数学模型、数学证明、数学符号。

normal.en: The family runs mathematical, mathematics, mathematician, mathematically, and the verb mathematize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学的、数学、数学家、在数学上，以及动词「使数学化」。

normal.en: The word can also criticise: to call an argument too mathematical is to say it ignores people.
normal.cn: 这个词也可用于批评：说一个论证太数学化，就是说它忽视了人。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a page so that every line must follow its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横在纸上，每一行都必须顺着它的边。

abstract.en: Picture a lock whose key is a proof: it opens only if every tumbler falls in order.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁，钥匙是一份证明：只有每个弹子依次落位，它才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge whose every stone was placed by calculation before anything was lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，每块石料在起吊之前就已由计算放好。

examples.en: The model is mathematical, so it can be tested on a computer.
examples.cn: 这个模型是数学性的，因此可以在计算机上检验。

examples.en: She has a mathematical mind and never loses track of a proof.
examples.cn: 她有数学头脑，推导从不迷失。

examples.en: The argument was mathematical in its precision, if not in its warmth.
examples.cn: 这个论证在精确上像数学，尽管并不温情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学问的」转成「数理的」：词根意为学习，学得最严的那一门 → 数学的、严密的

root: 希腊 mathēmatikos「爱学习的、有学问的」= mathēma「所学之物」+ 表示「属于」的后缀；拉丁 mathematicus 兼作形容词与名词，英语十六、十七世纪加形容词词尾；「精确严密」义由证明的声望引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one modifier: belonging to the discipline, using its tools, exact in reasoning, good with numbers, abstractly symbolic, modellable, formally proved, and finally as certain as arithmetic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个修饰语扇开：属于该学科、使用其工具、推理精确、数字能力强、抽象符号化、可建模、形式可证，最后是像算术一样确定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of derivation with boxes around each step and arrows from premise to conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页推导，每一步都加了方框，箭头从前提到结论。

branches.en: The field and its proof: what belongs to mathematics is settled by deduction, not by trial.
branches.cn: 学科与其证明：属于数学之事由演绎定案，而非靠试。

branches.en: The tool lent out: other subjects borrow equations to make themselves predictable.
branches.cn: 借出的工具：别的学科借方程来使自己可预测。

branches.en: Precision as a promise: no loose step, and a conclusion as certain as a sum.
branches.cn: 精确作为一种承诺：没有松掉的一步，结论像加法一样确定。

branches.en: The person: a mind that keeps its footing on a proof.
branches.cn: 人：在证明上不会失足的心智。

branches.en: The abstraction: the same quality turns into a criticism when it leaves people out.
branches.cn: 抽象：同一种品质一旦把人排除在外，就变成批评。

intro.en: The adjective is assembled from a Greek noun, a Greek suffix and a Latin adjectival ending, all of which also build its relatives.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊名词、希腊后缀与拉丁形容词词尾组成，这些部件也构成它的亲属词。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma supplies the meaning, -ikos marks belonging, and Latin -alis (English -al) turns it into an English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词提供意义，希腊后缀标记「属于」，拉丁形容词词尾把它转为英语形容词。

items.example: The root supplies the learned element of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「学问」成分。

items.example: The suffix made an adjective out of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the direct ancestor of the English one.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是英语形容词的直系祖先。

items.example: The Latin ending lets the Greek stem behave as an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词尾让希腊词干充当英语形容词。

items.example: The word describes whatever belongs to the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个词描述属于该领域之物。

items.example: The adverb marks how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记做某事的方式。

items.example: The noun names the field the adjective refers to.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名形容词所指的领域。

items.meaning: one who works in the field
items.example: The person suffix closes the family.
items.exampleCN: 表人后缀收拢了这个词族。

items.example: The verb names the act of turning something into mathematics.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把某物变成数学处理对象的行为。

latinEntries.structure: mathēma, mathēmatos (n., third declension, Greek loan)

definition_zh: 数学家；数学工作者；（旧时）占星术士
definition_en: a person who studies or works in mathematics; in earlier English, also a person who practised astrology
core_image: 书房里，一位研究者面前只有几张写满符号的纸，墙上小黑板还留着一条待证的命题
scene: 书房里，一位研究者面前的纸上只有符号与箭头，墙上的小黑板写着一个还没证完的命题。The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
sceneCN: 这里 mathematician 指「以研究数学为业的人」（第 1 个义项：从事数学研究的人）；句意为这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。图中可辨识物件：草稿纸、符号、小黑板、铅笔。

pos.zh: （十六、十七世纪用法）占星术士

senses.title: A researcher in mathematics
senses.definition: a person whose profession is to study or advance mathematics
senses.definitionCN: 以研究或推进数学为职业的人
senses.example: The mathematician worked for six years before the proof was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家做了六年，证明才被接受。
senses.why: The person suffix turns the field's name into the name of someone who works in it.
senses.whyCN: 表人后缀把学科之名变成从事该学科者之名。

senses.title: A teacher of the subject
senses.titleCN: 数学教师与数学工作者
senses.definition: a person who teaches mathematics or applies it as part of a job
senses.definitionCN: 教授数学、或在工作中的一部分运用数学的人
senses.example: The school hired a mathematician to run the advanced class.
senses.exampleCN: 学校聘请了一位数学工作者来带高级班。
senses.why: Teaching and applied work both count as living by the subject, so the word covers more than research alone.
senses.whyCN: 教书与应用工作都算靠这门学问谋生，因此这个词的覆盖面大于纯研究。

senses.title: Someone good with numbers
senses.titleCN: 擅长计算的人（宽泛说法）
senses.definition: used loosely of anyone unusually skilled at calculation
senses.definitionCN: 宽松地指任何在计算上特别熟练的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a mathematician to check that bill.
senses.exampleCN: 核对那张账单并不需要你是数学家。
senses.why: Everyday speech uses the word as a compliment for number sense, without insisting on formal training.
senses.whyCN: 日常说法用这个词称赞数字感，并不要求受过正式训练。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a person expert in a particular branch, such as geometry or number theory
senses.definitionCN: 精通某一分支（如几何或数论）的人
senses.example: The geometer and the analyst were both mathematicians, but they read different journals.
senses.exampleCN: 几何学家与分析学家都是数学家，但读的期刊不同。
senses.why: Branch names describe narrower expertise while the general word still applies to all of them.
senses.whyCN: 分支名称描述更窄的专长，而通名仍适用于其中所有人。

senses.title: A historical author of mathematical works
senses.titleCN: 历史上撰写数学著作的人
senses.definition: a historical figure known for written mathematical work rather than for a modern post
senses.definitionCN: 以数学著述而非现代职位闻名的历史人物
senses.example: The mathematician left a single book that was read for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这位数学家只留下一本书，却被读了几个世纪。
senses.why: History remembers people by their books, so the word attaches to authorship as much as to employment.
senses.whyCN: 历史按著作记住人，因此这个词既指职业，也指著述身份。

senses.title: An astrologer, in older usage
senses.definition: in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, a person who cast horoscopes and calculated celestial positions
senses.definitionCN: 在十六、十七世纪，指推算星盘与天体位置的人
senses.example: In Shakespeare's day a mathematician might be paid to read the stars.
senses.exampleCN: 在莎士比亚的时代，「数学家」可能受雇去读星象。
senses.why: Astronomy and astrology were then one body of calculation, and whoever did that calculation carried the name.
senses.whyCN: 当时天文与占星是一套计算，做这套计算的人便带着这个名号。

senses.title: A modeller in industry
senses.titleCN: 工业与金融中的数学建模人员
senses.definition: a person employed to build mathematical models for practical decisions
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为实际决策建立数学模型的人
senses.example: The insurer's mathematicians priced the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家保险公司的数学人员为新保单定了价。
senses.why: Outside academia the same training is sold as modelling, and the old word follows the skill.
senses.whyCN: 在学界之外，同样的训练以建模之名出售，旧词随技能而行。

senses.title: A calculating person, figuratively
senses.definition: used of someone who plans every move as if solving an equation
senses.definitionCN: 比喻把每一步都当作解方程来筹划的人
senses.example: A good negotiator is something of a mathematician about other people's motives.
senses.exampleCN: 好的谈判者对他人动机的把握颇有几分数学家的味道。
senses.why: The figurative use transfers the cool step-by-step manner of proof to social behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法把证明中那种冷静的逐步骤态度移用到社交行为上。

intro.en: The word is the name of the field plus a suffix for a person. Its Greek root means 'learning', and its early English sense could include astrology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由学科之名加表人后缀构成。其希腊词根意为「学习」，早期英语中还可指占星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mathēma 'something learned' came from manthanein 'to learn'; the deeper root is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: mathēma「所学之物」源自动词 manthanein「学习」；更深词根属重构形式，并无实证。

items.en: Latin mathematicus named a student of the mathematical studies, and in later usage could also mean an astrologer.
items.cn: 拉丁 mathematicus 指数学诸科的研习者，后世也可指占星者。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English used mathematic for the field itself, and the person's name was formed from it.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语用 mathematic 指这门学问本身，表人之名即由此构成。

items.en: The ending came into English through French from Latin -ianus, which marks someone connected with a thing.
items.cn: 这个表人词尾经法语来自拉丁 -ianus，标记与某事物有关联的人。

items.en: Because celestial prediction was then a branch of calculation, a mathematician could be hired to cast a horoscope; the sense faded as the two trades separated.
items.cn: 由于当时星象预测属于计算的一支，「数学家」可受雇推算星盘；随着两种行业分开，这一义项衰落。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word settled on the academic and industrial researcher. First date uncertain: no single year is recorded for the narrower modern sense.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词固定指学术与工业中的研究者。首见年代不确定：较窄的现代义没有确切年份记录。

note.en: Group one separates words that look alike but belong to different roots; group two separates the neighbouring specialists.
note.cn: 第一组辨析外形相近而词根不同的词；第二组辨析相邻的专门从业者。

entries.definition: An older adjective and singular noun for the field; it never names a person, though it looks like a shortened form of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的形容词与单数名词，指这门学问；它从不指人，尽管看起来像本词的缩短形式。

entries.definition: Describes work or ability rather than a person; 'a mathematical person' is not the same as 'a mathematician'.
entries.definitionCN: 描述工作或能力，而不指人；「有数学头脑的人」与「数学家」并不等同。

entries.definition: A person skilled in arithmetic, built on the Greek word for number rather than on the word for learning.
entries.definitionCN: 指精通算术的人，建立在希腊语表示数字的词上，而非表示学习的词上。

entries.definition: A specialist in geometry; the branch name plus the person suffix, parallel in form but narrower in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何学专家；分支名加表人后缀，形式平行而范围更窄。

entries.definition: One who works mainly with symbolic equations; a mathematician may never touch algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 主要指从事符号方程工作的人；数学家未必接触代数。

entries.definition: An older and more formal word for a worker in geometry, still used for classical studies of shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指几何工作者的更旧更正式的说法，仍用于对形的古典研究。

entries.definition: One who works with data and probability; the training overlaps but the daily work differs.
entries.definitionCN: 指处理数据与概率的人；训练有重叠，但日常工作不同。

entries.definition: One who calculates risk and premiums for insurers, using mathematics as a tool rather than as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 指为保险机构计算风险与保费的人，把数学当工具而非研究对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the field's name plus a person suffix, so it means one who lives by the field.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名加表人后缀，因此指靠这门学问谋生的人。

normal.en: The Greek root says 'learned', so the earliest bearers of the name were simply people of learning.
normal.cn: 希腊词根意为「有学问的」，因此最早带这个名号的人只是有学问者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: pure mathematician, applied mathematician, a team of mathematicians.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：纯数学家、应用数学家、一组数学家。

normal.en: In Shakespeare's time the same word could mean an astrologer, since star-reading was then calculation.
normal.cn: 在莎士比亚时代，同一个词可指占星者，因为读星象当时属于计算。

normal.en: The family runs mathematics, mathematical, mathematician, mathematically, plus the old form mathematic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括数学、数学的、数学家、在数学上，另有旧形式「数学的」。

abstract.en: Picture a person who fills a wall with a single proof and then sleeps beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把一整面墙写满同一个证明，然后就在旁边睡下。

abstract.en: Picture a locksmith who never touches a door but knows every lock in the city.
abstract.cn: 想象一位锁匠从不碰门，却熟悉全城每一把锁。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player who sees the board three moves before anyone else does.
abstract.cn: 想象一位棋手，比旁人早三步看见棋盘。

examples.en: The mathematician published the proof in a journal read by few.
examples.cn: 这位数学家把证明发表在一份读者很少的期刊上。

examples.en: Applied mathematicians now work closely with surgeons.
examples.cn: 应用数学家如今与外科医生密切合作。

examples.en: As a mathematician she distrusted any argument that skipped a step.
examples.cn: 作为数学家，她不信任任何跳过一步的论证。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「学数学的人」：学科名换上一个表人尾巴 → 数学家

root: 希腊 mathēma「所学之物」+ 拉丁 -ianus 表人后缀（经法语入英语）；拉丁 mathematicus 兼指数学研习者与占星者；十六、十七世纪英语中可指占星术士，十九世纪固定为现代数学家。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the researcher to the teacher, the number-skilled person, the branch specialist, the historical author, the old astrologer, the industrial modeller, and finally the calculating character of a negotiator.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从研究者，移到教师、擅长数字者、分支专家、历史著作者、旧时的占星者、工业建模者，最后到谈判者身上那种精于算计的气质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with symbol-covered pages and a small board holding an unfinished proof.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子，上面是写满符号的纸，旁边小黑板留着未完成的证明。

branches.en: Research and teaching: the same training spent either on new proofs or on other people's lessons.
branches.cn: 研究与教学：同样的训练，或用于新证明，或用于他人的课。

branches.en: Number sense, plain and figurative: a compliment at a till, a metaphor at a negotiating table.
branches.cn: 数字感，字面与比喻：收银台边的称赞，谈判桌上的隐喻。

branches.en: The narrow branch and the remembered book: expertise can be local or historical.
branches.cn: 窄分支与留存的书：专长可以是局部的，也可以是历史的。

branches.en: The old stars: the same name once covered those who read horoscopes.
branches.cn: 旧时的星：同一个名号曾涵盖读星盘的人。

branches.en: The market: the same skill sold as modelling for insurers and engineers.
branches.cn: 市场：同样的技能作为建模卖给保险与工程。

intro.en: The word is a Greek stem with a Greek adjective suffix, then a Latin person suffix, all of which also build the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊词干加希腊形容词后缀，再加拉丁表人后缀，这些部件也构成词族其余部分。

latinIntro.en: Greek mathēma supplies 'learning', -ikos marks belonging, and Latin -ianus (through French) marks a person.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语名词提供「学习」之义，希腊后缀标记「属于」，拉丁后缀经法语标记人。

items.example: The stem supplies the learning at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干提供词心处的「学问」。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into the adjective from which the person name is built.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词，再由它构成表人之名。

items.example: The Greek adjective is the base of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊形容词是英语名词的基础。

items.example: The Latin suffix marks a person associated with the field.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁后缀标记与该领域有关的人。

items.example: The English ending is the everyday person marker for trades and fields.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词尾是行业与领域的常用表人标记。

items.example: The word names the practitioner rather than the practice.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指从业者而非这门实践。

items.example: The field name is what the person name is built on.
items.exampleCN: 表人之名建立在学科名上。

items.example: The adjective describes the work rather than the worker.
items.exampleCN: 形容词描述工作而非工作者。

items.example: The adverb marks the manner of working.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记工作的方式。

latinEntries.structure: mathēma, mathēmatos (n., third declension, Greek loan)

definition_zh: 算术；四则运算；计算；（作定语）算术的
definition_en: the branch of mathematics that deals with counting and the basic operations of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division; also the act of calculating with numbers
core_image: 一张收据上列着几行数字，有人在页边用铅笔把每一行相加，最后画一条横线写下总数
scene: 餐桌上摊着一张收据，几行数字旁有人用铅笔逐行相加，画一道横线写下总数。Simple arithmetic showed that the month had cost more than the budget allowed.
sceneCN: 这里 arithmetic 指「加减乘除这类基本运算」（第 1 个义项：算术）；句意为简单的算术就算出这个月花得比预算多。图中可辨识物件：收据、铅笔、加号、横线、总数。

pos.zh: 算术的（如算术平均，重音后移）

senses.title: The branch of basic operations
senses.definition: the part of mathematics that handles counting and addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
senses.definitionCN: 数学中处理计数与加减乘除的部分
senses.example: Simple arithmetic showed that the month had cost more than the budget allowed.
senses.exampleCN: 简单的算术就算出这个月花得比预算多。
senses.why: The core sense names the oldest and most familiar layer of number work, the four operations on whole quantities.
senses.whyCN: 核心义指数字工作中最古老、最熟悉的一层，即对整数量的四则运算。

senses.title: The act of calculating
senses.definition: the process of working out a total or a difference with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字算出总数或差额的过程
senses.example: By his arithmetic, the trip would take eleven hours.
senses.exampleCN: 照他的计算，这趟要走十一个小时。
senses.why: The word shifts from the branch of study to the sums someone actually performs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从学问分支转到某人实际做的那些计算。

senses.title: The school subject and its drill
senses.definition: the early school subject in which children learn written and mental calculation
senses.definitionCN: 儿童学习笔算与心算的早期学校科目
senses.example: The class spent the whole morning on arithmetic.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班整个上午都在上算术。
senses.why: Because the operations are taught first, the word also names the school hour and the skill being drilled.
senses.whyCN: 由于这些运算最先被教授，这个词也指那节课与被反复训练的能力。

senses.title: The sums behind a situation
senses.titleCN: 某一局面背后的数字账
senses.definition: the numerical facts that decide whether a plan or a claim can hold
senses.definitionCN: 决定一项计划或说法能否成立的数字事实
senses.example: The arithmetic of the scheme fails once fuel is counted.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦把燃料算进去，这个方案的账就不成立了。
senses.why: Any plan rests on quantities, and the word names the quantities rather than the technique of counting.
senses.whyCN: 任何计划都靠数量支撑，这个词指那些数量，而非计数技巧。

senses.title: A plain reckoning of gains and losses
senses.definition: used figuratively for a hard, unemotional count of what is gained and lost
senses.definitionCN: 比喻冷静而不动感情地清点所得与所失
senses.example: The political arithmetic made the bill impossible to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 政治上的得失一算，这项法案就通不过。
senses.why: Politics borrows the word when a decision is settled by counting support rather than by argument.
senses.whyCN: 当一项决定靠清点支持者而非辩论来定案时，政治便借用这个词。

senses.title: Arithmetic as a modifier
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of the simple operations', as in arithmetic mean or arithmetic progression
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前表示「属基本运算的」，如算术平均、等差数列
senses.example: The arithmetic mean of the three readings is fourteen.
senses.exampleCN: 三个读数的算术平均是十四。
senses.why: The noun also serves as a modifier, at the cost of a stress shift in speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可充当修饰语，代价是口语中重音后移。

senses.title: Integer arithmetic in a machine
senses.definition: the fixed or floating operations a computer performs on stored numbers
senses.definitionCN: 计算机对存储数字进行的定点或浮点运算
senses.example: The bug came from integer arithmetic, not from the formula.
senses.exampleCN: 毛病出在整数运算，而不在公式。
senses.why: Machines reproduce the four operations under strict rules, so computing inherited the old word for them.
senses.whyCN: 机器在严格规则下重演四则运算，计算技术便继承了它们的旧名。

senses.title: One of the ancient four studies
senses.definition: in the medieval curriculum, the study of number as one of the four mathematical arts
senses.definitionCN: 中世纪课程中作为四门数学技艺之一的数据之学
senses.example: Boethius wrote a textbook of arithmetic that schools used for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 波爱修斯写过一本算术教材，学校用了几百年。
senses.why: The word entered Latin schooling as a named subject in the quadrivium, which is why it sounds older and more formal than 'sums'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词作为四艺中的一门具名科目进入拉丁学校课程，因此听起来比「算数」更古、更正式。

intro.en: The word goes back to Greek arithmos 'number' and the phrase for the art of counting. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到希腊语 arithmos「数」以及表示「计数之艺」的短语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arithmos meant 'number, count'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a verb meaning 'to fit together' is a hypothesis, and the root is usually given only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数、计数」。其更深来源不确定；把它与某个意为「拼合」的动词相联系的看法只是假说，其词根通常只以重构形式给出。

items.en: The phrase arithmētikē tekhnē, 'the art of counting', was shortened to arithmētikē and gave the adjective arithmētikos 'of counting'.
items.cn: 「计数之艺」这一短语被缩短为 arithmētikē，并给出形容词 arithmētikos「计数的」。

items.en: Latin arithmetica named the subject, and through Boethius it became one of the four mathematical arts of the medieval curriculum.
items.cn: 拉丁 arithmetica 成为学科之名，并经波爱修斯之手成为中世纪课程四门数学技艺之一。

items.en: The word reached English through French in the thirteenth century in forms such as arsmetrik, where the Latin word for 'art' was blended into the name.
items.cn: 这个词在十三世纪经法语进入英语，形式如 arsmetrik，其中拉丁语表示「技艺」的词被混进了名称里。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers restored the learned spelling arithmetic, and the modern word keeps that shape.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者恢复了学术拼写，现代词形沿用这一写法。

items.en: The school subject, the everyday sum, machine operations and the political count all grow from the same core. First date uncertain: the adjective use with shifted stress is recorded only from later centuries, with no agreed first year.
items.cn: 学校科目、日常算账、机器运算与政治清点都从同一核心长出。首见年代不确定：重音后移的形容词用法只见于更晚的世纪，没有公认的最早年份。

note.en: Group one separates words that look related but come from other roots; group two separates the everyday words for reckoning.
note.cn: 第一组辨析看似相关而词根不同的词；第二组辨析表示「计算」的日常词。

entries.definition: From the name of a medieval mathematician, not from the Greek word for number: it names a procedure, not the operations themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 来自一位中世纪数学家的名字，而非希腊语表示数字的词：它指一套步骤，而非运算本身。

entries.definition: Built from Greek logos 'ratio' plus arithmos 'number', so it is a relative of this word but names an exponent, not a sum.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语表示「比」的词加表示「数」的词构成，因此是本词的亲属，但指指数，而非求和。

entries.definition: The regular adjective of the subject; arithmetic itself can also be used before a noun, which causes confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 该科目的正规形容词；算术本身也可置于名词前，二者常致混淆。

entries.definition: The whole discipline, of which arithmetic is the oldest layer; the two words differ in root as well as in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 整个学科，算术是其中最早的一层；两词既在词根上不同，也在范围上不同。

entries.definition: Any worked-out reckoning, including algebra and estimation; arithmetic is its simplest and most concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 任何推算，包括代数与估算；算术是其中最简、最具体的形式。

entries.definition: Reckoning done by formal rules or by a machine, often on large amounts of data.
entries.definitionCN: 按形式规则或由机器完成的计算，常处理大量数据。

entries.definition: The practical ability to handle numbers and percentages in daily life; it is a skill, not a branch of study.
entries.definitionCN: 在日常生活中处理数字与百分比的实际能力；它是技能，而非学问分支。

entries.definition: In British speech, 'good at figures' means good at arithmetic; the plural noun stands in for the sums themselves.
