metrum, metri (n., second declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 三角学的；三角函数的；用三角比计算的
definition_en: relating to trigonometry, or to the functions of an angle such as sine, cosine and tangent
core_image: 一个单位圆上，一条半径转到某处，圆外的波形随之升降，角度与高度被一一对应
scene: 纸上画着一个单位圆，一条半径转到某处，圆外的波形随之升降，角度与高度被一一对应。The trigonometric functions repeat their values every full turn.
sceneCN: 这里 trigonometric 指「属于三角函数的」（第 2 个义项：三角函数意义上的）；句意为这些三角函数每转一整圈就重复一次取值。图中可辨识物件：单位圆、半径、波形、角度标记。

pos.zh: 三角学的；三角函数的；用三角比计算的

senses.title: Belonging to trigonometry
senses.definition: relating to the branch that studies the sides and angles of triangles
senses.definitionCN: 与研究三角形边角关系的分支有关
senses.example: The trigonometric identities are proved before they are used.
senses.exampleCN: 三角恒等式先被证明，然后才被使用。
senses.why: The plainest reading attaches the branch's name to whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 最朴素的用法把分支之名挂到所描述的对象上。

senses.title: Of the circular functions
senses.definition: describing the functions of an angle, sine, cosine and tangent, that map a turn to a ratio
senses.definitionCN: 描述把转角映射为比值的那类角函数，如正弦、余弦、正切
senses.example: The trigonometric functions repeat their values every full turn.
senses.exampleCN: 这些三角函数每转一整圈就重复一次取值。
senses.why: This is the sense in almost all technical writing, because the branch's daily work is done with functions rather than triangles.
senses.whyCN: 这是几乎所有技术文献中的义项，因为这门分支的日常工作靠函数而非三角形来完成。

senses.title: Computed by ratios
senses.definition: found by applying the ratios of sides to a known angle
senses.definitionCN: 把边的比值用于已知角而得出的
senses.example: The trigonometric solution gave the height in three lines.
senses.exampleCN: 三角解法三行就算出了高度。
senses.why: When a result is obtained by these ratios, the adjective marks the method of solution.
senses.whyCN: 当结果由这些比值得到时，这个形容词标记求解方法。

senses.title: Of triangulation surveys
senses.definition: describing the method of fixing positions by measuring angles between known points
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过测量已知点之间的夹角来定点的方法
senses.example: The trigonometric survey covered the whole valley in one season.
senses.exampleCN: 三角测量在一个季节里覆盖了整个山谷。
senses.why: Land measurement was the branch's origin, and the adjective still marks the practical technique.
senses.whyCN: 丈量土地是这门分支的源头，这个形容词仍标记那一实用技术。

senses.title: Of equations with those functions
senses.titleCN: 含三角函数的方程与恒等式的
senses.definition: describing equations or identities in which the unknown appears inside a trig function
senses.definitionCN: 描述未知量出现在三角函数之内的方程或恒等式
senses.example: The trigonometric equation has two solutions in one turn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个三角方程在一圈之内有两个解。
senses.why: Once functions entered algebra, equations needed a word to say what kind of unknown they contained.
senses.whyCN: 函数进入代数之后，方程需要一个词来说明其中含有何种未知量。

senses.title: Of series built from waves
senses.definition: describing a series of sine and cosine terms used to approximate a function
senses.definitionCN: 描述用正弦与余弦项逼近函数的级数
senses.example: The trigonometric series matched the signal almost exactly.
senses.exampleCN: 这个三角级数与信号几乎完全吻合。
senses.why: Because the functions repeat, adding them in series can rebuild any repeating shape.
senses.whyCN: 由于这些函数会重复，把它们逐项相加就能重建任何重复的形状。

senses.title: Of exact angular relations
senses.definition: describing relations stated in exact angles and ratios rather than estimates
senses.definitionCN: 描述以精确角度与比值陈述、而非估算的关系
senses.example: The linkage has a trigonometric exactness that the wooden model lacks.
senses.exampleCN: 这套连杆具有三角函数般的精确，木模型则没有。
senses.why: The adjective lends the exactness of the ratios to any description that uses them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把比值的精确性借给任何使用它们的描述。

senses.title: Of periodic behaviour
senses.definition: describing change that repeats at regular intervals, as these functions do
senses.definitionCN: 描述按固定间隔重复的变化，正如这些函数
senses.example: Tides have a trigonometric rhythm, twice a day and twice a month.
senses.exampleCN: 潮汐有三角函数式的节律，一天两次，一月两次。
senses.why: The functions became the standard language for cycles, so the adjective now marks periodicity itself.
senses.whyCN: 这些函数成了描述周期的标准语言，因此这个形容词如今标记周期性本身。

intro.en: The adjective is the sixteenth-century Latin name of the branch plus an adjectival ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是十六世纪这门分支的拉丁名称加形容词词尾。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trigonon 'triangle' combined tri- 'three' with gōnia 'angle'; the earlier origin of gōnia is reconstructed.
items.cn: trigonon「三角形」由表示「三」的前缀与表示「角」的词合成；表示角的词更早来源属重构形式。

items.en: Metron 'measure' named the second half of the compound, the same element found in geometry.
items.cn: metron「量度」命名复合词的后半，与几何一词中所见相同。

items.en: A sixteenth-century treatise title built trigonometria from those two Greek nouns, using Latin word formation.
items.cn: 十六世纪一部论著的标题用拉丁构词法把这两个希腊名词造成 trigonometria。

items.en: The Latin adjective trigonometricus followed the noun, and English took both forms together.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词随后出现，英语把名词与形容词一并借入。

items.en: Seventeenth- and eighteenth-century English used the adjective for tables, functions and surveys.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪的英语用这个形容词修饰表、函数与测量。

items.en: The sense 'of the circular functions' became dominant once analysis replaced table-work. First date uncertain: this shift was gradual and has no agreed first citation.
items.cn: 「属于圆函数的」这一义项在分析取代查表之后占据主导。首见年代不确定：这一转移是渐进的，没有公认的最早书证。

note.en: Group one separates the adjective from the same family; group two separates other adjectives of measurement.
note.cn: 第一组辨析这个形容词与同族形式；第二组辨析其他测量类形容词。

entries.definition: The branch itself; the adjective differs only by its ending, which is easy to miss in a scan.
entries.definitionCN: 指分支本身；形容词只差词尾，扫读时容易漏看。

entries.definition: A longer adjective common in older texts; modern technical writing prefers the shorter form.
entries.definitionCN: 较早文献中常见的较长形容词；现代技术写作多用较短形式。

entries.definition: The adverb modifies verbs of solving or measuring, not nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 副词修饰求解或测量的动词，而非名词。

entries.definition: Of geometry rather than trigonometry; the two adjectives often sit side by side in the same sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 属于几何而非三角学；两个形容词常在同一句里并排出现。

entries.definition: Describes anything that repeats at fixed intervals; trigonometric functions are the classic examples.
entries.definitionCN: 描述按固定间隔重复之物；三角函数是经典例子。

entries.definition: Concerned with angles themselves rather than with ratios of sides.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及角本身，而非边之比。

entries.definition: Describes a curve of the sine shape; trigonometric covers the whole family of such functions.
entries.definitionCN: 描述正弦形状的曲线；三角的一词涵盖这一整族函数。

entries.definition: Relating to map-making, a field that consumes trigonometric results without being trigonometry.
entries.definitionCN: 与制图有关；制图消耗三角成果，但本身不是三角学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective is the branch name with an ending, so it marks whatever the ratios are applied to.
normal.cn: 这个形容词是分支名加词尾，因此标记那些比值所施加的对象。

normal.en: Its four home phrases are function, identity, equation and table.
normal.cn: 它的四个常用搭配是函数、恒等式、方程与表。

normal.en: The family runs trigonometric, trigonometry, trigonometrical, trigonometrically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括三角的、三角学、较长形容词、用三角方法。

normal.en: Sine and cosine turn a turning arm into two smooth waves, which is why the word now means periodic.
normal.cn: 正弦与余弦把一条旋转的臂变成两条平滑的波，因此这个词如今也指周期性的。

normal.en: Surveyors were the first to use the ratios at ground level, fixing positions by angles alone.
normal.cn: 测量员最早在地面上使用这些比值，仅凭角度定点。

abstract.en: Picture a radius sweeping round a circle while a pen outside traces its height up and down.
abstract.cn: 想象一条半径绕圆扫过，圆外一支笔随之把它的高度画上画下。

abstract.en: Picture a lighthouse beam turning at a steady rate, its light arriving on a fixed rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象灯塔的光束匀速旋转，光按固定节律抵达。

abstract.en: Picture a table of numbers consulted by lamplight to find a distance no rope could reach.
abstract.cn: 想象就着灯光查一张数字表，为的是求一段绳索量不到的距离。

examples.en: Every trigonometric identity can be derived from the unit circle.
examples.cn: 每个三角恒等式都能从单位圆推出。

examples.en: The engineers used a trigonometric method to align the mirror.
examples.cn: 工程师用三角方法校准镜面。

examples.en: Trigonometric tables were printed long before calculators existed.
examples.cn: 三角数表在计算器出现之前很久就已印行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「三角测量的」：三角学名称加形容词尾巴 → 三角的、三角函数的

root: 新拉丁 trigonometria 为十六世纪以希腊部件所造：trigonon「三角形」+ metron「量度」；其形容词随之进入英语，十七、十八世纪用于表、函数与测量，分析兴起后「圆函数」义成为主流。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one adjective: of the branch, of the circular functions, solved by ratios, used in triangulation, appearing inside equations, summed in series, exact in angular terms, and finally marking any periodic rhythm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个形容词铺开：属于分支、属于圆函数、由比值求解、用于三角测量、出现在方程之内、级数求和、角度上精确，最后标记任何周期节律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a radius sweeping a circle while a curve outside rises and falls with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条半径扫过圆，圆外的曲线随之升降。

branches.en: The branch and its ratios: what belongs to trigonometry is solved by proportion.
branches.cn: 分支与其比值：属于三角学之事由比例求解。

branches.en: Function and equation: a turn becomes a value, and that value becomes an unknown.
branches.cn: 函数与方程：转角变成取值，取值又变成未知量。

branches.en: The field and its exactness: positions fixed by angles, and relations stated without estimates.
branches.cn: 实地与精确：用角定点，以及不用估算陈述的关系。

branches.en: The series: repeating terms added until any shape is rebuilt.
branches.cn: 级数：重复的项相加，直到任何形状被重建。

branches.en: The rhythm: the same functions become the language of every cycle.
branches.cn: 节律：同一批函数成了每个周期的语言。

intro.en: The adjective carries three Greek pieces and a Latin ending, all of them shared with the noun it modifies.
intro.cn: 这个形容词带着三个希腊部件与一个拉丁词尾，它们都与它所修饰的名词共用。

latinIntro.en: Tri- counts, gōnia names the angle, metron names the measure; Latin -icus makes the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀数出数目，表示角的词命名角，表示量度的词命名量度；拉丁词尾构成形容词。

items.example: The prefix fixes the number of angles in the name.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀定下名称中角的数目。

items.example: The angle element names what is observed.
items.exampleCN: 角的成分命名被观测之物。

items.example: The noun supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的前半。

items.example: The measuring element supplies the second half.
items.exampleCN: 量度成分提供后半。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of belonging.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示归属的形容词。

items.example: Latin formed the adjective on the model of geometricus.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语仿几何形容词的样式构成它。

items.example: English uses it almost always before function, identity or equation.
items.exampleCN: 英语几乎总把它放在函数、恒等式或方程之前。

items.example: Older texts use the longer adjective.
items.exampleCN: 较早文献用较长形容词。

items.example: The adverb marks how a result was obtained.
items.exampleCN: 副词标记结果的获得方式。

definition_zh: 微积分；演算体系；（体内）结石
definition_en: the branch of mathematics that studies continuous change through derivatives and integrals; also a system of calculation, or a hard mass formed in the body
core_image: 一只碗里堆着几颗小石子，旁边是一张记满刻痕的木板，石子被一颗颗拨动来记数
scene: 桌上一只碗里堆着几颗小石子，旁边是一块刻满记号的木板，有人把石子一颗颗拨过去记数。The doctor found a small calculus in the patient's kidney.
sceneCN: 这里 calculus 指「体内形成的结石」（第 4 个义项：结石）；句意为医生在病人肾脏里发现一颗小结石。图中可辨识物件：碗、小石子、刻痕木板、拨动的手。

senses.title: The mathematics of continuous change
senses.titleCN: 研究连续变化的微积分
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that studies rates of change and accumulated totals by means of derivatives and integrals
senses.definitionCN: 用导数与积分研究变化率与累积总量的数学分支
senses.example: Calculus turned the problem of motion into a problem of rates.
senses.exampleCN: 微积分把运动问题化为变化率问题。
senses.why: The core sense is a system of computation built for quantities that change smoothly rather than in steps.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一套为平滑变化（而非逐级跳变）的量而建的计算体系。

senses.title: The course in it
senses.definition: the university course in which differentiation and integration are taught
senses.definitionCN: 教授微分与积分的大学课程
senses.example: Calculus is the gate through which most science students must pass.
senses.exampleCN: 微积分是多数理科学生必须通过的关口。
senses.why: A branch taught to large numbers of students becomes a named course, and the word follows the timetable.
senses.whyCN: 一门教给大量学生的学问成为具名课程，这个词也随之进入课表。

senses.title: A cold reckoning
senses.definition: used of a hard calculation of costs and benefits in which feelings play no part
senses.definitionCN: 指不计感情、只算得失的冷酷算计
senses.example: The firm's calculus was simple: two hundred jobs against one factory.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的算账很简单：两百个岗位对一座工厂。
senses.why: The figurative use borrows the word for any system of computation, then strips it of mathematics and leaves only the coldness.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法借用任何计算体系之名，再抽掉数学，只留下那份冷。

senses.title: A stone in the kidney
senses.definition: a hard mass formed from minerals in the kidney or bladder
senses.definitionCN: 由矿物质在肾或膀胱中形成的坚硬块状物
senses.example: The doctor found a small calculus in the patient's kidney.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在病人肾脏里发现一颗小结石。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a small pebble, and medical writers used it for stones formed in the body because the resemblance was exact.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指小石子，医学作者用它指体内形成的石头，因为两者形状确实相似。

senses.title: Hard deposit on teeth
senses.definition: a hardened layer of mineral deposit on the surface of a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 牙齿表面矿化变硬的沉积层
senses.example: Dental calculus has to be removed by a hygienist.
senses.exampleCN: 牙结石必须由洁牙师清除。
senses.why: The same pebble image extends to any hard mineral crust, and dentistry took it for the deposit on teeth.
senses.whyCN: 同一个石子意象扩展到任何坚硬矿壳，牙科取它指牙面上的沉积。

senses.title: A formal system of inference
senses.definition: a set of symbols and rules for deriving statements, as in the propositional or predicate calculus
senses.definitionCN: 由符号与规则组成、用于推出命题的体系，如命题演算或谓词演算
senses.example: The predicate calculus made the argument checkable by machine.
senses.exampleCN: 谓词演算使这个论证可以由机器检验。
senses.why: Logicians wanted a word for rule-governed symbol manipulation, and borrowed the mathematicians' word for a computing system.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学家需要一个词指按规则摆弄符号，于是借用了数学家的「计算体系」一词。

senses.title: A system of calculation in general
senses.definition: any organised method of computing according to fixed rules
senses.definitionCN: 任何按固定规则进行计算的成体系方法
senses.example: Every calculus is a machine made of rules rather than wheels.
senses.exampleCN: 每一套演算都是用规则而非齿轮做成的机器。
senses.why: The word's older and wider sense simply names an organised way of reckoning, before it was attached to any one branch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词更旧更宽的义项只是命名一种成体系的算法，尚未绑定到某一分支。

senses.title: The pebble used for counting
senses.definition: in Latin, a small stone moved on a counting board to keep a tally
senses.definitionCN: 在拉丁语中指在算板上拨动以记数的小石子
senses.example: Roman accountants moved calculi across a board instead of writing figures.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马的账房拨动算板上的石子，而不写数字。
senses.why: The whole family of words about calculation begins with a handful of pebbles.
senses.whyCN: 整套关于计算的词，都从一把小石子开始。

intro.en: The word is Latin for a small pebble, and it came to name both stones in the body and systems of calculation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁语中意为小石子，后来既指体内结石，也指计算体系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Calx meant 'limestone, chalk'. Its origin is not established, and the forms offered for it in older etymologies are reconstructions.
items.cn: calx 意为「石灰岩、白垩」。其来源未得到证明，较早词源学为其给出的形式均属重构。

items.en: The diminutive calculus named a small stone or pebble, the kind moved on a counting board.
items.cn: 指小形式 calculus 指小石头或卵石，正是算板上被拨动的那一种。

items.en: From the pebbles came calculare 'to reckon' and the whole later family of words about calculation.
items.cn: 由这些石子生出表示「计算」的动词，以及后来整套与计算有关的词。

items.en: Medical Latin used calculus for a hard mass formed in the body; English keeps this sense in renal and dental use.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 calculus 指体内形成的硬块；英语在肾结石与牙结石中保留这一义项。

items.en: Newton and Leibniz each built a method for rates and totals, and the Latin word for a system of computation was chosen to name it.
items.cn: 牛顿与莱布尼茨各自建立了处理变化率与总量的方法，人们选用拉丁语中表示计算体系的词来命名。

items.en: English now uses the singular for the branch and the Latin plural calculi for stones, so the two senses are kept apart by their plurals. First date uncertain: the logic sense spread through nineteenth- and twentieth-century textbooks with no single coining.
items.cn: 英语如今用单数指分支，用拉丁复数 calculi 指结石，两个义项靠复数形式分开。首见年代不确定：逻辑义经十九、二十世纪教科书扩散，并无单次命名。

note.en: Group one separates near forms of the same root; group two separates other mathematical systems.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同根近形词；第二组辨析其他数学体系。

entries.definition: To work something out by arithmetic; it comes from the same pebble root but names the act, not the branch.
entries.definitionCN: 指用算术算出某事；同出石子词根，但指行为而非分支。

entries.definition: The process or outcome of reckoning; it lacks the technical meaning of a formal system.
entries.definitionCN: 计算的过程或结果；不含「形式体系」这一技术义。

entries.definition: A device that performs arithmetic; the suffix marks an instrument rather than a body of mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 执行算术运算的装置；词尾标记器械而非数学体系。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of the nature of a stone', used in medicine; it looks like the noun but is a describing word.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「结石性的」医学形容词；看起来像名词，实为描述词。

entries.definition: Solves equations by rearranging symbols; calculus instead handles change and accumulation.
entries.definitionCN: 通过重排符号解方程；微积分处理的则是变化与累积。

entries.definition: The modern branch that contains calculus together with limits, series and functions; calculus is its introductory core.
entries.definitionCN: 包含微积分以及极限、级数与函数的现代分支；微积分是它的入门核心。

entries.definition: Works with fixed numbers and the four operations; it has no notion of a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 用固定数字做四则运算；没有极限的概念。

entries.definition: Studies figures and space; calculus supplies the tools for curves and areas that geometry alone cannot total.
entries.definitionCN: 研究图形与空间；微积分为几何单独无法求总的曲线与面积提供工具。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin word is a small pebble, so every word about calculation began with stones moved on a board.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁词就是小石子，因此一切关于计算的词都起于算板上被拨动的石子。

normal.en: The same pebble named the stone in a kidney, which is why medicine and mathematics share one spelling.
normal.cn: 同一颗石子也命名肾中的石头，因此医学与数学共用一个拼写。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both lives of the word: differential calculus, integral calculus, renal calculus, dental calculus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这个词的两世：微分学、积分学、肾结石、牙结石。

normal.en: The plural separates the senses: one form for systems, another for stones.
normal.cn: 复数把义项分开：体系义与结石义各用不同的复数形式。

normal.en: A calculus is a machine made of rules, which is why logicians borrowed the name for formal inference.
normal.cn: 一套演算是用规则做成的机器，因此逻辑学家借这个名称指形式推演。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl of pebbles and a board of tally marks, the first computer.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗石子与一块刻满记号的板，那是最早的计算机。

abstract.en: Picture a curve cut into strips so thin that each strip is almost a rectangle, then all added.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线被切成极薄的条，每条几乎是一个矩形，然后把它们相加。

abstract.en: Picture a committee deciding lives by columns of figures, with no faces in the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会按几列数字决定人的去留，屋里没有一张脸。

examples.en: Calculus is required for the physics major.
examples.cn: 物理专业要求学微积分。

examples.en: The surgeon removed a calculus from the duct.
examples.cn: 外科医生从导管中取出一颗结石。

examples.en: Their calculus ignored every cost that could not be counted.
examples.cn: 他们的算计忽略了所有无法计数的代价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「小石子」：拉丁语小石子，算板上拨石记数 → 计算体系 → 微积分、结石

root: 拉丁 calx「石灰岩」的指小形式 calculus「小石子」，本指算板上记数用的石子，由此生出「计算」一族词；医学拉丁语借指体内结石；十七世纪牛顿与莱布尼茨的方法借「计算体系」之名，遂成微积分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a handful of pebbles: the branch of change, its course, a cold reckoning, a kidney stone, a deposit on teeth, a formal system of inference, any rule-governed computation, and the pebble itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一把小石子展开：研究变化的分支、其课程、冷酷的算计、肾结石、牙结石、形式推演体系、任何按规则的计算，以及那颗石子本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl of pebbles beside a tally board, each stone moved to keep count.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只碗的石子放在记数板旁，每颗都被拨动以记数。

branches.en: The branch and the general system: calculus is one organised way of computing, raised to a whole subject.
branches.cn: 分支与一般体系：微积分是一种成体系的算法，被提升为一门学科。

branches.en: The course and the cold sum: one taught in a hall, one done in a boardroom with no faces.
branches.cn: 课程与冷酷算账：一在大教室被教，一在会议室里做，后者没有脸孔。

branches.en: The stone in the body: kidney and tooth, both named after a pebble.
branches.cn: 体内的石头：肾与牙，都以石子为名。

branches.en: The formal system: rules for deriving statements, borrowed from the computing sense.
branches.cn: 形式体系：推演的规则，借自计算义。

branches.en: The pebble itself, where the whole family starts.
branches.cn: 石子本身，整族词的起点。

intro.en: The word is a Latin diminutive, so its shape is root plus a suffix meaning 'little'; every English relative keeps that root.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁指小形式，形状为词根加表示「小」的后缀；每个英语亲属词都保留这个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin calx 'limestone' gives the root, -culus makes it a small stone, and calculare turns the stone into the act of reckoning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示石灰岩的词给出词根，指小后缀把它变成小石子，动词又把石子变成计算的行为。

items.example: The root names the material of which the pebbles were made.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名石子所用的材料。

items.example: The suffix shrinks the material into a single pebble.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把材料缩小成一颗石子。

items.example: The diminutive is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个指小形式是整族词的基础。

items.example: The verb turns the object into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把对象变成活动。

items.example: English keeps the everyday verb from the same pebble.
items.exampleCN: 英语从这个石子得到日常动词。

items.meaning: the act or result of reckoning
items.example: The noun names what the verb does.
items.exampleCN: 名词命名动词所做之事。

items.meaning: full of or caused by stones
items.example: The adjective belongs to the medical sense only.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词只属于医学义。

items.example: The Latin plural keeps the medical sense separate.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁复数把医学义单独保留。

items.example: The phrase shows the borrowing by logic.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语显示逻辑学对它的借用。

latinEntries.meaning: a pebble; a stone in the body

definition_zh: 方程；等式；（需权衡的）因素；均衡
definition_en: a mathematical statement that two expressions are equal; also a situation in which several factors must be balanced
core_image: 一张纸上左右两边各堆着几项，中间一个等号，两边的项被逐个搬动，直到只剩一个字母
scene: 纸上左右两边各堆着几项，中间一个等号，两边的项被逐项搬动，直到只剩一个字母。The equation balances only if both sides are treated alike.
sceneCN: 这里 equation 指「两边相等的方程」（第 1 个义项：含未知量的等式）；句意为只有两边同等对待，这个方程才平衡。图中可辨识物件：等号、两边的项、被搬动的符号、孤立的字母。

pos.zh: 方程；等式；均衡；需考虑的因素

collocations.phrase: the equation of supply and demand

senses.title: A statement with an equals sign
senses.definition: a mathematical statement asserting that two expressions have the same value
senses.definitionCN: 断言两个式子取值相同的数学陈述
senses.example: The equation balances only if both sides are treated alike.
senses.exampleCN: 只有两边同等对待，这个方程才平衡。
senses.why: The core sense is a written claim of equality, holding an unknown in place until it is solved.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个写下来的相等主张，把未知量固定住，直到它被解出。

senses.title: Equality as a relation
senses.definition: the relation of being equal in value, size or amount
senses.definitionCN: 在取值、大小或数量上相等的关系
senses.example: The equation between the two totals was a coincidence.
senses.exampleCN: 两个总数相等只是巧合。
senses.why: The word can name the relation rather than the statement, which is why it also appears in non-mathematical comparisons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指关系而非陈述，因此也出现在非数学的比较中。

senses.title: A chemical equation
senses.definition: a symbolic statement that the atoms of the reactants equal those of the products
senses.definitionCN: 用符号陈述反应物原子与生成物原子相等
senses.example: The chemical equation shows two hydrogen molecules for every one of oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 这个化学方程式显示每一分子氧对应两分子氢。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the form of a mathematical equality to express conservation of matter.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了数学等式的形式来表达物质守恒。

senses.title: One factor among several
senses.definition: used of something that must be taken into account when a decision is weighed
senses.definitionCN: 指在权衡决定时必须纳入考虑的东西
senses.example: Cost was only one factor in the equation.
senses.exampleCN: 成本只是这个局面的一个因素。
senses.why: When a decision is described as an equation, every factor becomes a term that must be balanced against the others.
senses.whyCN: 当一项决定被说成一个方程时，每个因素都成为须与其余项相平衡的项。

senses.title: A state of balance
senses.definition: a condition in which opposing forces or quantities are made equal
senses.definitionCN: 对立的力量或数量被调到相等的状态
senses.example: The treaty sought an equation of naval strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约谋求海军力量的均衡。
senses.why: The older sense names the act or state of making things equal, rather than the written form that records it.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项指使事物相等的行为或状态，而非记录它的书面形式。

senses.title: A law written as a relation
senses.definition: a formula expressing a physical or chemical law as an equality between quantities
senses.definitionCN: 把物理或化学定律写成量之间相等关系的公式
senses.example: The equation of state links pressure, volume and temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 状态方程把压力、体积与温度联系起来。
senses.why: Once a law is written as an equality, it is called an equation, even when nothing is being solved.
senses.whyCN: 一条定律一旦写成相等式，就被称作方程，尽管并没有在解什么。

senses.title: A situation reduced to two sides
senses.titleCN: 把局面化为等号两边的模型
senses.definition: a simplified model in which a complicated situation is treated as two sides that must match
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂局面当作必须相符的两边来处理的简化模型
senses.example: The planner reduced the problem to an equation: land on one side, people on the other.
senses.exampleCN: 规划者把问题化成一个方程：一边是土地，一边是人。
senses.why: Modelling borrows the equals sign because it forces a balance that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 建模借用等号，因为它逼出一个可以核对的平衡。

senses.title: An astronomical correction
senses.titleCN: 天文中使观测与平均相等的校正量
senses.definition: historically, the amount by which an observed value must be adjusted to match a mean value, as in the equation of time
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指为使观测值符合平均值而作的校正量，如时差
senses.example: The equation of time can differ from the clock by a quarter of an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 时差可以使日晷与钟表相差一刻钟。
senses.why: Early astronomy used the word for a correction that equalises two reckonings, before it settled on the algebraic sense.
senses.whyCN: 早期天文学用这个词指使两种算法相等的校正，早于它固定为代数义。

intro.en: The word goes back to Latin aequus 'level, equal', through the verb 'to make equal'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 aequus「平的、相等的」，经表示「使相等」的动词而来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均匀的、相等的」。其更深来源未得到证明，为其提出的形式均属重构。

items.en: Aequare 'to make level or equal' turned the adjective into a verb of balancing.
items.cn: aequare「使平、使相等」把这个形容词变成表示平衡的动词。

items.en: Aequatio named a making equal or a distribution, and medieval Latin used it for the statement of an equality.
items.cn: aequatio 指使相等或分配，中世纪拉丁语用它指相等关系的陈述。

items.en: English took equation in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, first in astronomy for corrections and later for algebraic statements.
items.cn: 英语在十六、十七世纪吸收这个词，先用在天文学指校正，后用于代数陈述。

items.en: The sign of two parallel lines was chosen in the sixteenth century because no two things could be more equal, and the written equation followed.
items.cn: 两条平行线的符号于十六世纪被选用，因为再没有两样东西能比它们更相等；书面方程随之成形。

items.en: Chemistry applied the form to reactions, and everyday speech applied it to decisions. First date uncertain: the figurative 'factor in the equation' is a twentieth-century development with no agreed first use.
items.cn: 化学把这一形式用于反应，日常说法把它用于决定。首见年代不确定：「方程中的一个因素」这一比喻是二十世纪的发展，没有公认的最早用例。

note.en: Group one separates words from the same root; group two separates other mathematical statements.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同根词；第二组辨析其他数学陈述。

entries.definition: To treat two things as equal; the noun names the statement, the verb names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指把两物视为相等；名词指陈述，动词指行为。

entries.definition: The state of being equal, often social rather than mathematical; an equation is a written claim of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指相等的状态，常用指社会平等而非数学；方程是这种相等关系的书面主张。

entries.definition: Means even-tempered or steady, from the idea of level; it has nothing to do with solving.
entries.definitionCN: 意为性情平和或稳定，来自「平」的观念；与求解无关。

entries.definition: The line that divides the globe equally; it looks like a relative of equation but belongs to geography.
entries.definitionCN: 把地球平分的线；看起来像方程的同族词，实则属于地理。

entries.definition: A general expression of a relation, often with known symbols; an equation asserts equality for a particular case.
entries.definitionCN: 关系的一般表达式，多用已知符号；方程则为某一情形断言相等。

entries.definition: An equality that holds for every value of the variables, unlike an equation to be solved.
entries.definitionCN: 对所有变量取值都成立的等式，区别于待解的方程。

entries.definition: A combination of symbols with no equals sign; it becomes part of an equation when set against another.
entries.definitionCN: 不含等号的符号组合；与另一式相对时才成为方程的一部分。

entries.definition: A statement that one side is greater or smaller; it replaces the equals sign with a direction.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述一边大于或小于另一边；它用方向取代等号。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means level, so an equation is a claim that the two sides sit at the same height.
normal.cn: 词根意为「平」，因此方程是主张两边处在同一高度的陈述。

normal.en: The equals sign was chosen as two parallel lines because nothing could be more equal than they are.
normal.cn: 等号被选为两条平行线，因为没有东西能比它们更相等。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its homes: solve an equation, a linear equation, a chemical equation, equation of state.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的去处：解方程、一次方程、化学方程式、状态方程。

normal.en: The family runs equation, equate, equating, equational, equality.
normal.cn: 同族词包括方程、使相等、等同、等式的、相等。

normal.en: As a figure of speech, every factor in a decision becomes a term that must be balanced.
normal.cn: 作为比喻，一项决定里的每个因素都成为必须配平的项。

abstract.en: Picture a balance scale whose two pans must hold the same weight before it rests.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两盘必须承同样的重量它才静止。

abstract.en: Picture a budget with income on one side and every obligation listed on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预算，一边是收入，另一边列着全部义务。

abstract.en: Picture a sundial and a clock disagreeing by a quarter of an hour, and someone correcting one to match the other.
abstract.cn: 想象日晷与钟表差了一刻钟，有人把其中一个校正到与另一个相符。

examples.en: The equation has no solution in whole numbers.
examples.cn: 这个方程没有整数解。

examples.en: Write the chemical equation for the reaction.
examples.cn: 写出这个反应的化学方程式。

examples.en: Time, not money, was the missing factor in the equation.
examples.cn: 这个局面里缺的因素是时间，而不是钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「让两边变平」：拉丁语「平、相等」加名词词尾 → 等式、方程

root: 拉丁 aequus「平的、相等的」→ aequare「使相等」→ aequatio「使相等、相等关系的陈述」；英语十六、十七世纪先用于天文校正，后指代数等式；等号为十六世纪所选的两条平行线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one image, two sides level with each other: the written equation, the relation of equality, a chemical balance, a factor to be weighed, a state of balance, a law written as equality, a situation reduced to two sides, and an astronomical correction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都落在同一个意象上，即两边齐平：写下的方程、相等关系、化学配平、须权衡的因素、均衡状态、写成等式的一条定律、被化为两边的局面，以及天文上的校正量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: terms stacked on either side of one equals sign, moved until a single letter is left alone.
core.cn: 核心意象：等号两边各堆着若干项，被搬动到只剩一个字母独自站着。

branches.en: The written claim and the relation it records: a statement, and equality itself.
branches.cn: 写下的主张与它所记录的关系：一个陈述，以及相等本身。

branches.en: Chemistry and law: both write a balance as an equality that must hold.
branches.cn: 化学与定律：两者都把一种平衡写成必须成立的等式。

branches.en: Decisions and models: factors become terms, and a tangle becomes two sides.
branches.cn: 决定与模型：因素成为项，一团乱麻变成两边。

branches.en: The older balance: forces or quantities brought level with one another.
branches.cn: 较旧的平衡：力量或数量被调到彼此齐平。

branches.en: The correction: an observed value adjusted until it matches a mean.
branches.cn: 校正：观测值被调到与平均值相符。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective turned into a verb and then into a noun, so the whole family shares one root meaning level.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁形容词先转动词、再转名词，因此整族词共享一个意为「平」的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus 'level' gives aequare 'to make level', and aequatio names the resulting equality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「平」的词给出「使平」动词，名词则命名由此得到的相等。

items.example: The root carries the image of two surfaces at one height.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着两个面处于同一高度的意象。

items.example: The verb names the act of bringing things level.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把事物调平的行为。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成行为名词。

items.meaning: a making equal; an equality stated
items.example: Medieval Latin used it for written equalities.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语用它指写下的相等关系。

items.example: English keeps both the algebraic and the balancing senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语既保留代数义，也保留平衡义。

items.example: The verb returns the noun to action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把名词还原为行为。

items.example: The abstract noun generalises the relation.
items.exampleCN: 抽象名词把这个关系一般化。

items.example: The adjective marks whatever belongs to written equalities.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记属于书面等式之物。

items.meaning: a law stated as an equality
items.example: The phrase shows the sense of a law, not a problem.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语显示的是定律义，而非待解问题。
